23.s: athābhiṣekasya vidhiḥ kathyate pārameśvaraḥ // 1
23.d: अथाभिषेकस्य विधिः कथ्यते पारमेश्वरः ॥ 1
23.m: Now the supreme lordly ritual of consecration is explained. // 1

23.s:
yaiṣā putrakadīkṣoktā gurusādhakayorapi /
saivādhikāriṇī bhogyatattvayuktimatī kramāt // 2
23.d:
यैषा पुत्रकदीक्षोक्ता गुरुसाधकयोरपि ।
सैवाधिकारिणी भोग्यतत्त्वयुक्तिमती क्रमात् ॥ 2
23.m:
This initiation that was taught for the spiritual son serves also for the guru and the adept,
conferring authority and endowed with application to the respective objects of enjoyment in succession. // 2

23.s:
svabhyastajñāninaṃ santaṃ bubhūṣumatha bhāvinam /
yogyaṃ jñātvā svādhikāraṃ gurustasmai samarpayet // 3
23.d:
स्वभ्यस्तज्ञानिनं सन्तं बुभूषुमथ भाविनम् ।
योग्यं ज्ञात्वा स्वाधिकारं गुरुस्तस्मै समर्पयेत् ॥ 3
23.m:
Knowing that someone well-practiced in knowledge is virtuous, desirous of becoming [a teacher], or an eminent candidate,
and knowing him fit, the guru should bestow his own authority upon him. // 3

23.s:
yo naivaṃ veda naivāsāvabhiṣikto'pi daiśikaḥ /
samayyādikrameṇeti śrīmatkāmika ucyate // 4
23.d:
यो नैवं वेद नैवासावभिषिक्तोऽपि दैशिकः ।
समय्यादिक्रमेणेति श्रीमत्कामिक उच्यते ॥ 4
23.m:
One who does not know thus is not a master at all, even if consecrated
in the sequence of initiate into the rule and the rest; so it is said in the venerable Kāmika. // 4

23.s:
yo na vedādhvasandhānaṃ ṣoḍhā bāhyāntarasthitam /
sa gururmocayenneti siddhayogīśvarīmate // 5
23.d:
यो न वेदाध्वसन्धानं षोढा बाह्यान्तरस्थितम् ।
स गुरुर्मोचयेन्नेति सिद्धयोगीश्वरीमते ॥ 5
23.m:
One who does not know the unification of the path situated sixfold externally and internally,
that guru cannot liberate; thus [it is taught] in the Siddhayogīśvarīmata. // 5

23.s:
sarvalakṣaṇahīno'pi jñānavān gururiṣyate /
jñānaprādhānyamevoktamiti śrīkacabhārgave // 6
23.d:
सर्वलक्षणहीनोऽपि ज्ञानवान् गुरुरिष्यते ।
ज्ञानप्राधान्यमेवोक्तमिति श्रीकचभार्गवे ॥ 6
23.m:
Even if devoid of all physical characteristics, one endowed with knowledge is accepted as a guru;
the preeminence of knowledge alone has been declared in the venerable Kacabhārgava: // 6

23.s:
padavākyapramāṇajñaḥ śivabhaktyekatatparaḥ /
samastaśivaśāstrārthaboddhā kāruṇiko guruḥ // 7
23.d:
पदवाक्यप्रमाणज्ञः शिवभक्त्येकतत्परः ।
समस्तशिवशास्त्रार्थबोद्धा कारुणिको गुरुः ॥ 7
23.m:
'Knowing words, sentences, and pramāṇas, solely dedicated to devotion to Śiva,
understanding the meaning of all Śiva scriptures, compassionate is the guru.' // 7

23.s:
na svayaṃbhūstasya coktaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ parameśinā /
abhakto jīvitadhiyā kurvannīśānadhiṣṭhitaḥ // 8
23.d:
न स्वयंभूस्तस्य चोक्तं लक्षणं परमेशिना ।
अभक्तो जीवितधिया कुर्वन्नीशानधिष्ठितः ॥ 8
23.m:
A self-appointed guru is not [valid], and his characteristic has been taught by the Supreme Lord:
'Undevoted, acting out of a desire for livelihood, possessed by the Lord of the bound souls,

23.s:
paścātmanā svayaṃbhūṣṇurnādhikārī sa kutracit /
bhasmāṅkuro vratisuto duḥśīlātanayastathā // 9
23.d:
पश्चात्मना स्वयंभूष्णुर्नाधिकारी स कुत्रचित् ।
भस्माङ्कुरो व्रतिसुतो दुःशीलातनयस्तथा ॥ 9
23.m:
desiring to become [a guru] by his own self afterward—he has no authority anywhere.'
One with an ash-mark, a son of an ascetic, a son of an immoral woman,

23.s:
kuṇḍo golaśca te duṣṭā uktaṃ devyākhyayāmale /
punarbhūścānyaliṅgo yaḥ punaḥ śaive pratiṣṭhitaḥ // 10
23.d:
कुण्डो गोलश्च ते दुष्टा उक्तं देव्याख्ययामले ।
पुनर्भूश्चान्यलिङ्गो यः पुनः शैवे प्रतिष्ठितः ॥ 10
23.m:
a kuṇḍa, and a gola—these are unfit, as taught in the Devyāyāmala;
and a re-initiate, one who held another mark and is then established in the Śaiva fold. // 10

23.s:
śrīpūrvaśāstre na tveṣa niyamaḥ ko'pi coditaḥ /
yathārthatattvasaṃghajñastathā śiṣye prakāśakaḥ // 11
23.d:
श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे न त्वेष नियमः कोऽपि चोदितः ।
यथार्थतत्त्वसंघज्ञस्तथा शिष्ये प्रकाशकः ॥ 11
23.m:
In the venerable Pūrvaśāstra, however, no such rule whatsoever is enjoined:
'One who knows the real collection of principles, and illuminates them likewise in the disciple,

23.s:
yaḥ punaḥ sarvatattvāni vettītyādi ca lakṣaṇam /
yogacāre ca yadyatra tantre coditamācaret // 12
23.d:
यः पुनः सर्वतत्त्वानि वेत्तीत्यादि च लक्षणम् ।
योगचारे च यद्यत्र तन्त्रे चोदितमाचरेत् ॥ 12
23.m:
and who furthermore knows all principles'—and such are the characteristics.
And whatever is prescribed in this or that Tantra regarding practice,

23.s:
tathaiva siddhaye seyamājñeti kila varṇitam /
yastu karmitayācāryastatra kāṇādivarjanam // 13
23.d:
तथैव सिद्धये सेयमाज्ञेति किल वर्णितम् ।
यस्तु कर्मितयाचार्यस्तत्र काणादिवर्जनम् ॥ 13
23.m:
just that is described as the command leading to accomplishment.
As for the exclusion of one-eyed persons and the like in the case of a ritualist master,

23.s:
yataḥ kārakasāmagryātkarmaṇo nādhikaḥ kvacit /
devyā yāmalaśāstre ca kāñcyādiparivarjanam // 14
23.d:
यतः कारकसामग्र्यात्कर्मणो नाधिकः क्वचित् ।
देव्या यामलशास्त्रे च काञ्च्यादिपरिवर्जनम् ॥ 14
23.m:
because ritual action nowhere exceeds the collection of instrumental factors;
and the exclusion of those from Kāñcī and elsewhere in the Devyāyāmala scripture,

23.s:
taddṛṣṭadoṣātkrodhādeḥ samyakjñātaryasau kutaḥ /
guravastu svayaṃbhvādi varjyaṃ yadyāmalādiṣu // 15
23.d:
तद्दृष्टदोषात्क्रोधादेः सम्यक्ज्ञातर्यसौ कुतः ।
गुरवस्तु स्वयंभ्वादि वर्ज्यं यद्यामलादिषु ॥ 15
23.m:
that is due to the visible defects seen in them, such as anger; how could that apply to one who properly knows?
As for what is taught in the Yāmala and other texts as to be avoided, such as the self-appointed,

23.s:
karmyabhiprāyataḥ sarvaṃ taditi vyācacakṣire /
ato deśakulācāradehalakṣaṇakalpanām // 16
23.d:
कर्म्यभिप्रायतः सर्वं तदिति व्याचचक्षिरे ।
अतो देशकुलाचारदेहलक्षणकल्पनाम् ॥ 16
23.m:
the gurus explained that all this is with reference to the ritualist.
Therefore, completely disregarding considerations of region, family custom, and bodily marks,

23.s:
anādṛtyaiva saṃpūrṇajñānaṃ kuryādgururgurum /
prāgvatsaṃpūjya hutvā ca śrāvayitvā cikīrṣitam // 17
23.d:
अनादृत्यैव संपूर्णज्ञानं कुर्याद्गुरुर्गुरुम् ।
प्राग्वत्संपूज्य हुत्वा च श्रावयित्वा चिकीर्षितम् ॥ 17
23.m:
the guru should make one possessing complete knowledge a guru.
Having worshiped and offered oblation as before, and having proclaimed what is to be done,

23.s:
tato'bhiṣiñcettaṃ śiṣyaṃ catuḥṣaṣṭyā tataḥ sakṛt /
tanmantrarasatoyena pūrvoktavidhinā guruḥ // 18
23.d:
ततोऽभिषिञ्चेत्तं शिष्यं चतुःषष्ट्या ततः सकृत् ।
तन्मन्त्ररसतोयेन पूर्वोक्तविधिना गुरुः ॥ 18
23.m:
the guru should then consecrate that disciple sixty-four times, and then once,
with water infused with the essence of that mantra, according to the rule previously explained. // 18

23.s:
vibhavena suvistīrṇaṃ tatastasmai vadetsvakam /
sarvaṃ kartavyasāraṃ yacchāstrāṇāṃ paramaṃ rahaḥ // 19
23.d:
विभवेन सुविस्तीर्णं ततस्तस्मै वदेत्स्वकम् ।
सर्वं कर्तव्यसारं यच्छास्त्राणां परमं रहः ॥ 19
23.m:
Then, with extensive grandeur, he should communicate to him his own
entire essence of duties, which is the supreme secret of the scriptures: // 19

23.s:
anugrāhyāstvayā śiṣyāḥ śivaśaktipracoditāḥ /
uktaṃ jñānottare caitadbrāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā viśaḥ // 20
23.d:
अनुग्राह्यास्त्वया शिष्याः शिवशक्तिप्रचोदिताः ।
उक्तं ज्ञानोत्तरे चैतद्ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया विशः ॥ 20
23.m:
'Disciples impelled by the power of Śiva are to be graced by you.'
And this is stated in the Jñānottara: 'Brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas,

23.s:
napuṃsakāḥ striyaḥ śūdrā ye cānye'pi tadarthinaḥ /
te dīkṣāyāṃ na mīmāṃsyā jñānakāle vicārayet // 21
23.d:
नपुंसकाः स्त्रियः शूद्रा ये चान्येऽपि तदर्थिनः ।
ते दीक्षायां न मीमांस्या ज्ञानकाले विचारयेत् ॥ 21
23.m:
eunuchs, women, śūdras, and whoever else seeks that—
they are not to be scrutinized at the time of initiation; he should examine them at the time of knowledge.' // 21

23.s:
jñānamūlo guruḥ proktaḥ saptasatrīṃ pravartayet /
dīkṣā vyākhyā kṛpā maitrī śāstracintā śivaikatā // 22
23.d:
ज्ञानमूलो गुरुः प्रोक्तः सप्तसत्रीं प्रवर्तयेत् ।
दीक्षा व्याख्या कृपा मैत्री शास्त्रचिन्ता शिवैकता ॥ 22
23.m:
The guru is declared to be rooted in knowledge; he should set in motion the seven sacrifices:
initiation, exposition, compassion, friendliness, reflection on the scriptures, oneness with Śiva, // 22

23.s:
annādidānamityetatpālayetsaptasatrakam /
abhiṣekavidhau cāsmai karaṇīkhaṭikādikam // 23
23.d:
अन्नादिदानमित्येतत्पालयेत्सप्तसत्रकम् ।
अभिषेकविधौ चास्मै करणीखटिकादिकम् ॥ 23
23.m: he should observe this sevenfold session consisting of gifts of food and the like. / And in the rite of consecration, the trowel, chalk, and other implements—

23.s:
sarvopakaraṇavrātamarpaṇīyaṃ vipaścite /
so'bhiṣikto guruṃ paścāddakṣiṇābhiḥ prapūjayet // 24
23.d:
सर्वोपकरणव्रातमर्पणीयं विपश्चिते ।
सोऽभिषिक्तो गुरुं पश्चाद्दक्षिणाभिः प्रपूजयेत् ॥ 24
23.m: the entire collection of ritual paraphernalia—should be handed over to the wise initiate. / He, once consecrated, should afterwards worship the guru with fees.

23.s:
jñānahīno guruḥ karmī svādhikāraṃ samarpya no /
dīkṣādyadhikṛtiṃ kuryādvinā tasyājñayā punaḥ // 25
23.d:
ज्ञानहीनो गुरुः कर्मी स्वाधिकारं समर्प्य नो ।
दीक्षाद्यधिकृतिं कुर्याद्विना तस्याज्ञया पुनः ॥ 25
23.m: A ritualist guru devoid of knowledge, once he has handed over his authority, / must not exercise authority such as initiation again without that [consecrated initiate's] command.

23.s:
ityevaṃ śrāvayetso'pi namaskṛtyābhinandayet /
tataḥ prabhṛtyasau pūrvo gurustyaktādhikārakaḥ // 26
23.d:
इत्येवं श्रावयेत्सोऽपि नमस्कृत्याभिनन्दयेत् ।
ततः प्रभृत्यसौ पूर्वो गुरुस्त्यक्ताधिकारकः ॥ 26
23.m: In this manner he should instruct [him]; having bowed, he should also congratulate him. / From then on, that previous guru has relinquished his authority.

23.s:
yathecchaṃ vicaredvyākhyādīkṣādau yantraṇojjhitaḥ /
kurvanna bādhyate yasmāddīpāddīpavadīdṛśaḥ // 27
23.d:
यथेच्छं विचरेद्व्याख्यादीक्षादौ यन्त्रणोज्झितः ।
कुर्वन्न बाध्यते यस्माद्दीपाद्दीपवदीदृशः ॥ 27
23.m: He may wander as he pleases, free from constraints regarding exposition, initiation, and the like; / for in performing [them] he is not obstructed, since such a one is like a lamp [lit] from a lamp.

23.s:
santāno nādhikārasya cyavo'kurvanna bādhyate /
prāk ca kurvanvihanyeta siddhātantre taducyate // 28
23.d:
सन्तानो नाधिकारस्य च्यवोऽकुर्वन्न बाध्यते ।
प्राक् च कुर्वन्विहन्येत सिद्धातन्त्रे तदुच्यते ॥ 28
23.m: There is a continuity [of power], not a loss of authority; in not performing [them], he is not hindered, / and in performing [them] previously he would be impaired—thus it is taught in the Siddhātantra.

23.s:
yathārthamupadeśaṃ tu kurvannācārya ucyate /
na cāvajñā kriyākāle saṃsāroddharaṇaṃ prati // 29
23.d:
यथार्थमुपदेशं तु कुर्वन्नाचार्य उच्यते ।
न चावज्ञा क्रियाकाले संसारोद्धरणं प्रति ॥ 29
23.m: One who gives genuine teaching, however, is called an ācārya; / and there should be no contempt [shown to him] at the time of ritual action regarding deliverance from saṃsāra.

23.s:
na dīkṣeta guruḥ śiṣyaṃ tattvayuktastu garvataḥ /
yo'sya syānnarake vāsa iha ca vyādhito bhavet // 30
23.d:
न दीक्षेत गुरुः शिष्यं तत्त्वयुक्तस्तु गर्वतः ।
योऽस्य स्यान्नरके वास इह च व्याधितो भवेत् ॥ 30
23.m: A guru, though endowed with true reality, must not out of pride initiate a disciple; / if he does, his dwelling will be in hell, and here [in this life] he will become diseased.

23.s:
prāptābhiṣekaḥ sa guruḥ ṣaṇmāsānmantrapaddhatim /
sarvāṃ tantroditāṃ dhyāyejjapeccātanmayatvataḥ // 31
23.d:
प्राप्ताभिषेकः स गुरुः षण्मासान्मन्त्रपद्धतिम् ।
सर्वां तन्त्रोदितां ध्यायेज्जपेच्चातन्मयत्वतः ॥ 31
23.m: Having received consecration, that guru should, for six months, contemplate and recite / the entire manual of mantras taught in the tantra, because he has not yet identified with it.

23.s:
yadaiva tanmayībhūtastadā vīryamupāgataḥ /
chindyātpāśāṃstato yatnaṃ kuryāttanmayatāsthitau // 32
23.d:
यदैव तन्मयीभूतस्तदा वीर्यमुपागतः ।
छिन्द्यात्पाशांस्ततो यत्नं कुर्यात्तन्मयतास्थितौ ॥ 32
23.m: Only when he has identified with it does he attain its potency; / then he may sever the bonds. Therefore he should strive to abide in identification with it.

23.s:
hṛccakrādutthitā sūkṣmā śaśisphaṭikasaṃnibhā /
lekhākārā nādarūpā praśāntā cakrapaṅktigā // 33
23.d:
हृच्चक्रादुत्थिता सूक्ष्मा शशिस्फटिकसंनिभा ।
लेखाकारा नादरूपा प्रशान्ता चक्रपङ्क्तिगा ॥ 33
23.m: Arising from the heart wheel, subtle, resembling the moon and crystal, / having the form of a line, consisting of sound (nāda), tranquil, moving through the series of wheels,

23.s:
dvādaśānte nirūḍhā sā sauṣumne tripathāntare /
tatra hṛccakramāpūrya japenmantraṃ jvalatprabham // 34
23.d:
द्वादशान्ते निरूढा सा सौषुम्ने त्रिपथान्तरे ।
तत्र हृच्चक्रमापूर्य जपेन्मन्त्रं ज्वलत्प्रभम् ॥ 34
23.m: firmly established in the twelve-finger space (dvādaśānta), within the three-pathed channel of suṣumṇā: / there, filling the heart wheel, he should recite the mantra blazing with radiance,

23.s:
cakṣurlomādirandhraughavahajjvālaurvasaṃnibham /
yāvacchāntaśikhākīrṇaṃ viśvājyapravilāpakam // 35
23.d:
चक्षुर्लोमादिरन्ध्रौघवहज्ज्वालौर्वसंनिभम् ।
यावच्छान्तशिखाकीर्णं विश्वाज्यप्रविलापकम् ॥ 35
23.m: resembling submarine fire with flames pouring out from the multitude of apertures such as eyes and hair pores, / filled with tranquil crests [of flame], liquefying the universe as its clarified butter,

23.s:
tadājyadhārāsaṃtṛptamānābhikuharāntaram /
evaṃ mantrā mokṣadāḥ syurdīptā buddhāḥ sunirmalāḥ // 36
23.d:
तदाज्यधारासंतृप्तमानाभिकुहरान्तरम् ।
एवं मन्त्रा मोक्षदाः स्युर्दीप्ता बुद्धाः सुनिर्मलाः ॥ 36
23.m: satisfied by that stream of clarified butter up to the hollow cavity of the navel. / In this way the mantras, blazing, awakened, and utterly pure, bestow liberation.

23.s:
mūlakandanabhonābhihṛtkaṇṭhālikatālugam /
ardhendurodhikānādatadantavyāpiśaktigam // 37
23.d:
मूलकन्दनभोनाभिहृत्कण्ठालिकतालुगम् ।
अर्धेन्दुरोधिकानादतदन्तव्यापिशक्तिगम् ॥ 37
23.m: Traversing the root-bulb, the sky [aperture], the navel, the heart, the throat, the forehead, and the palate, / reaching the crescent moon, the obstructress, the sound, the end of sound, the all-pervasive, and śakti,

23.s:
samanonmanaśuddhātmaparacakrasamāśritam /
yatra yatra japeccakre samastavyastabhedanāt // 38
23.d:
समनोन्मनशुद्धात्मपरचक्रसमाश्रितम् ।
यत्र यत्र जपेच्चक्रे समस्तव्यस्तभेदनात् ॥ 38
23.m: resorting to the supreme wheel of the pure Self, samanā, and unmanā— / wherever in a wheel he recites, by differentiating the collective and the discrete,

23.s:
tatra tatra mahāmantra iti devyākhyayāmale /
vidyāvratamidaṃ proktaṃ mantravīryaprasiddhaye // 39
23.d:
तत्र तत्र महामन्त्र इति देव्याख्ययामले ।
विद्याव्रतमिदं प्रोक्तं मन्त्रवीर्यप्रसिद्धये ॥ 39
23.m: there, indeed, is the great mantra—so it is taught in the Devyākhyayāmala. / This observance of Vidyā (vidyāvrata) is declared for the perfection of mantra potency,

23.s:
tacca tādātmyameveti yaduktaṃ spandaśāsane /
tadākramya balaṃ mantrāḥ sarvajñabalaśālinaḥ // 40
23.d:
तच्च तादात्म्यमेवेति यदुक्तं स्पन्दशासने ।
तदाक्रम्य बलं मन्त्राः सर्वज्ञबलशालिनः ॥ 40
23.m: and that is precisely identity [with consciousness], as stated in the Spanda teaching: / “Having seized that power, mantras, possessing the power of the omniscient,

23.s:
pravartante'dhikārāya karaṇānīva dehinām /
kṛtavidyāvrataḥ paścāddīkṣāvyākhyādi sarvataḥ // 41
23.d:
प्रवर्तन्तेऽधिकाराय करणानीव देहिनाम् ।
कृतविद्याव्रतः पश्चाद्दीक्षाव्याख्यादि सर्वतः ॥ 41
23.m: proceed to their respective function, like the sense faculties of embodied beings.” / Having completed the observance of Vidyā, he should thereafter everywhere perform initiation, exposition, and the like

23.s:
kuryādyogyeṣu śiṣyeṣu nāyogyeṣu kadācana /
rahasye yojayedvipraṃ parīkṣya viparītataḥ // 42
23.d:
कुर्याद्योग्येषु शिष्येषु नायोग्येषु कदाचन ।
रहस्ये योजयेद्विप्रं परीक्ष्य विपरीततः ॥ 42
23.m: upon worthy disciples, never upon the unworthy. / He should admit a brahmin to the secret teaching having tested him thoroughly, [or] conversely;

23.s:
ācārācchaktimapyeva nānyathetyūrmiśāsane /
nityādyalpālpakaṃ kuryādyaduktaṃ brahmayāmale // 43
23.d:
आचाराच्छक्तिमप्येव नान्यथेत्यूर्मिशासने ।
नित्याद्यल्पाल्पकं कुर्याद्यदुक्तं ब्रह्मयामले ॥ 43
23.m: and likewise a woman (śakti) on account of her conduct, not otherwise—thus in the Ūrmiśāsana. / He should perform the daily and other rites in minimal form, as is stated in the Brahmayāmala:

23.s:
cīrṇavidyāvrataḥ sarvaṃ manasā vā smaretpriye /
dehasaṃbandhasaṃchannasārvajñyo dambhabhājanam // 44
23.d:
चीर्णविद्याव्रतः सर्वं मनसा वा स्मरेत्प्रिये ।
देहसंबन्धसंछन्नसार्वज्ञ्यो दम्भभाजनम् ॥ 44
23.m: “One who has performed the observance of Vidyā, O dear one, may remember everything mentally.” / One whose omniscience is concealed by association with the body is a vessel of hypocrisy.

23.s:
avidandīkṣamāṇo'pi na duṣyeddaiśikaḥ kvacit /
jñātvā tvayogyatāṃ nainaṃ dīkṣeta pratyavāyitām // 45
23.d:
अविदन्दीक्षमाणोऽपि न दुष्येद्दैशिकः क्वचित् ।
ज्ञात्वा त्वयोग्यतां नैनं दीक्षेत प्रत्यवायिताम् ॥ 45
23.m: A master, even if initiating while unknowing, would not incur fault anywhere; / but knowing [the candidate’s] unworthiness, he should not initiate him, [lest he incur] transgression.

23.s:
buddhvā jñāne śāstrasiddhigurutvādau ca taṃ punaḥ /
bhūya eva parīkṣeta tattadaucityaśālinam // 46
23.d:
बुद्ध्वा ज्ञाने शास्त्रसिद्धिगुरुत्वादौ च तं पुनः ।
भूय एव परीक्षेत तत्तदौचित्यशालिनम् ॥ 46
23.m: Having discerned [him] in knowledge, in scriptural attainment, in guruship, and the like, / he should further test him again as one possessing this or that propriety;

23.s:
tatra tatra niyuñjīta natu jātu viparyayāt /
nanu tadvastvayogyasya tatrecchā jāyate kutaḥ // 47
23.d:
तत्र तत्र नियुञ्जीत नतु जातु विपर्ययात् ।
ननु तद्वस्त्वयोग्यस्य तत्रेच्छा जायते कुतः ॥ 47
23.m: he should employ him in those respective [duties], and never in reverse. / [Objection:] But how can a desire for that arise in one who is unworthy of the object?

23.s:
tadīśādhiṣṭhitecchaiva yogyatāmasya sūcayet /
satyaṃ kāpi prabuddhāsāvicchā rūḍhiṃ na gacchati // 48
23.d:
तदीशाधिष्ठितेच्छैव योग्यतामस्य सूचयेत् ।
सत्यं कापि प्रबुद्धासाविच्छा रूढिं न गच्छति ॥ 48
23.m: [Reply:] His desire itself, governed by the Lord, would indicate his worthiness. / True, but a desire that is awakened somewhere may fail to take root,

23.s:
vidyudvatpāpaśīlasya yathā pāpāpavarjane /
rūḍhyarūḍhī tadicchāyā api śaṃbhuprasādataḥ // 49
23.d:
विद्युद्वत्पापशीलस्य यथा पापापवर्जने ।
रूढ्यरूढी तदिच्छाया अपि शंभुप्रसादतः ॥ 49
23.m: like lightning, in a sinful person, regarding the abandonment of sin. / The rooting or non-rooting of that desire also comes from the grace of Śambhu;

23.s:
aprarūḍhatathecchākastata eva na bhājanam /
yaḥ samyagjñānamādāya guruviśvāsavarjitaḥ // 50
23.d:
अप्ररूढतथेच्छाकस्तत एव न भाजनम् ।
यः सम्यग्ज्ञानमादाय गुरुविश्वासवर्जितः ॥ 50
23.m: one whose desire has not taken root is, for that very reason, not a worthy recipient. / He who, having received right knowledge, is devoid of faith in the guru

23.s:
lokaṃ viplāvayennāsmiñjñāte vijñānamarpayet /
ajñāte'pi punarjñāte vijñānaharaṇaṃ caret // 51
23.d:
लोकं विप्लावयेन्नास्मिञ्ज्ञाते विज्ञानमर्पयेत् ।
अज्ञातेऽपि पुनर्ज्ञाते विज्ञानहरणं चरेत् ॥ 51
23.m: and would cause confusion among the people—one should not impart higher knowledge (vijñāna) to him if this is known. / Even if [imparted when] unknown, once it is known, one should perform the withdrawal of knowledge.

23.s:
punaḥpunaryadā jñāto viśvāsaparivarjitaḥ /
tadā tamagrato dhyāyetsphurantaṃ candrasūryavat // 52
23.d:
पुनःपुनर्यदा ज्ञातो विश्वासपरिवर्जितः ।
तदा तमग्रतो ध्यायेत्स्फुरन्तं चन्द्रसूर्यवत् ॥ 52
23.m: When he is recognized again and again as being devoid of faith, / then one should meditate on him in front, shining like the moon and the sun.

23.s:
tato nijahṛdambhojabodhāmbarataloditām /
svarbhānumalināṃ dhyāyedvāmāṃ śaktiṃ vimohanīm // 53
23.d:
ततो निजहृदम्भोजबोधाम्बरतलोदिताम् ।
स्वर्भानुमलिनां ध्यायेद्वामां शक्तिं विमोहनीम् ॥ 53
23.m: Then, one should meditate on the confusing Vāmā Śakti, arising from the firmament of consciousness in one's own lotus heart, / dark like Rāhu.

23.s:
vāmācārakrameṇaināṃ niḥsṛtāṃ sādhyagāminīm /
cintayitvā tayā grastaprakāśaṃ taṃ vicintayet // 54
23.d:
वामाचारक्रमेणैनां निःसृतां साध्यगामिनीम् ।
चिन्तयित्वा तया ग्रस्तप्रकाशं तं विचिन्तयेत् ॥ 54
23.m: Having visualized Her emerging by the course of the leftward movement and proceeding toward the target, / one should contemplate him as having his light consumed by Her.

23.s:
anena kramayogena mūḍhabuddherdurātmanaḥ /
vijñānamantravidyādyāḥ prakurvantyapakāritām // 55
23.d:
अनेन क्रमयोगेन मूढबुद्धेर्दुरात्मनः ।
विज्ञानमन्त्रविद्याद्याः प्रकुर्वन्त्यपकारिताम् ॥ 55
23.m: By this systematic process, for that wicked person of deluded intellect, / the higher knowledge, mantras, spells, and the rest bring about harm.

23.s:
nanu vijñānamātmasthaṃ kathaṃ hartuṃ kṣamaṃ bhavet /
ato vijñānaharaṇaṃ kathaṃ śrīpūrva ucyate // 56
23.d:
ननु विज्ञानमात्मस्थं कथं हर्तुं क्षमं भवेत् ।
अतो विज्ञानहरणं कथं श्रीपूर्व उच्यते ॥ 56
23.m: [Objection:] Surely, how could it be possible to withdraw knowledge that resides in oneself? / Therefore, how is the withdrawal of knowledge stated in the revered Pūrvaśāstra?

23.s:
ucyate nāsya śiṣyasya vijñānaṃ rūḍhimāgatam /
tathātve haraṇaṃ kasmātpūrṇayogyatvaśālinaḥ // 57
23.d:
उच्यते नास्य शिष्यस्य विज्ञानं रूढिमागतम् ।
तथात्वे हरणं कस्मात्पूर्णयोग्यत्वशालिनः ॥ 57
23.m: [Reply:] It is explained: this disciple’s higher knowledge has not taken root; / if it were so, why would there be withdrawal from one possessing complete worthiness?

23.s:
kiṃtveṣa vāmayā śaktyā mūḍho gāḍhaṃ vibhoḥ kṛtaḥ /
svabhāvādeva tenāsya vidyādyamapakārakam // 58
23.d:
किंत्वेष वामया शक्त्या मूढो गाढं विभोः कृतः ।
स्वभावादेव तेनास्य विद्याद्यमपकारकम् ॥ 58
23.m: Rather, he is rendered thoroughly deluded by the Lord’s Vāmā Śakti; / by its very nature, therefore, vidyā and the like become harmful to him.

23.s:
guruḥ punaḥ śivābhinnaḥ sanyaḥ pañcavidhāṃ kṛtim /
kuryādyadi tataḥ pūrṇamadhikāritvamasya tat // 59
23.d:
गुरुः पुनः शिवाभिन्नः सन्यः पञ्चविधां कृतिम् ।
कुर्याद्यदि ततः पूर्णमधिकारित्वमस्य तत् ॥ 59
23.m: Moreover, if the guru, being nondifferent from Śiva, / performs the fivefold activity, then his authority is complete.

23.s:
ato yathā śuddhatattvasṛṣṭisthityormalātyaye /
yojanānugrahe kāryacatuṣke'dhikṛto guruḥ // 60
23.d:
अतो यथा शुद्धतत्त्वसृष्टिस्थित्योर्मलात्यये ।
योजनानुग्रहे कार्यचतुष्केऽधिकृतो गुरुः ॥ 60
23.m: Therefore, just as the guru is authorized in the fourfold task: / creation and maintenance of the pure tattvas, destroying impurity, integration (yojana), and grace,

23.s:
śivābhedena tatkuryāttadvatpañcamamapyayam /
tirobhāvābhidhaṃ kṛtyaṃ tathāsau śivatātmakaḥ // 61
23.d:
शिवाभेदेन तत्कुर्यात्तद्वत्पञ्चममप्ययम् ।
तिरोभावाभिधं कृत्यं तथासौ शिवतात्मकः ॥ 61
23.m: which he performs through non-differentiation with Śiva, so too [he performs] this fifth / task called concealment (tirobhāva); thus he has the nature of Śiva.

23.s:
ata eva śive śāstre jñāne cāśvāsabhājanam /
gurormūḍhatayā kopadhāmāpi na tirohitaḥ // 62
23.d:
अत एव शिवे शास्त्रे ज्ञाने चाश्वासभाजनम् ।
गुरोर्मूढतया कोपधामापि न तिरोहितः ॥ 62
23.m: For this reason, one who has faith in Śiva, in scripture, and in knowledge / is not concealed even if he is the object of the guru’s anger due to delusion.

23.s:
gururhi kupito yasya sa tirohita ucyate /
saṃsārī satu devo hi gururna ca mṛṣāvidaḥ // 63
23.d:
गुरुर्हि कुपितो यस्य स तिरोहित उच्यते ।
संसारी सतु देवो हि गुरुर्न च मृषाविदः ॥ 63
23.m: For he with whom the guru is angry is called concealed; / he is a transmigrating soul (saṃsārī), for the guru is God, and those who know are not mistaken.

23.s:
tata eva ca śāstrādidūṣako yadyapi krudhā /
na dahyate'sau guruṇā tathāpyeṣa tirohitaḥ // 64
23.d:
तत एव च शास्त्रादिदूषको यद्यपि क्रुधा ।
न दह्यतेऽसौ गुरुणा तथाप्येष तिरोहितः ॥ 64
23.m: And for that very reason, even if a reviler of scriptures and the like is not burned / by the guru in wrath, he is nevertheless concealed.

23.s:
asmadgurvāgamastveṣa tirobhūte svayaṃ śiśau /
na kupyenna śapeddhīmān sa hyanugrāhakaḥ sadā // 65
23.d:
अस्मद्गुर्वागमस्त्वेष तिरोभूते स्वयं शिशौ ।
न कुप्येन्न शपेद्धीमान् स ह्यनुग्राहकः सदा ॥ 65
23.m: The tradition of our guru, however, is this: when a child [disciple] has himself become concealed, / the wise [guru] should not become angry and should not curse; for he is ever the bestower of grace.

23.s:
īśecchācoditaḥ pāśaṃ yadi kaṇṭhe nipīḍayet /
kimācāryeṇa tatrāsya kāryā syātsahakāritā // 66
23.d:
ईशेच्छाचोदितः पाशं यदि कण्ठे निपीडयेत् ।
किमाचार्येण तत्रास्य कार्या स्यात्सहकारिता ॥ 66
23.m: If, impelled by the Lord’s will, a person tightens the noose around his own neck, / why should the ācārya cooperate with him in that?

23.s:
śivābhinno'pi hi gururanugrahamayīṃ vibhoḥ /
mukhyāṃ śaktimupāsīno'nugṛhṇīyātsa sarvathā // 67
23.d:
शिवाभिन्नोऽपि हि गुरुरनुग्रहमयीं विभोः ।
मुख्यां शक्तिमुपासीनोऽनुगृह्णीयात्स सर्वथा ॥ 67
23.m: For even though non-different from Śiva, the guru, attending upon the primary / grace-filled power of the all-pervading Lord, should bestow grace by every means.

23.s:
svātantryamātrajñaptyai tu kathitaṃ śāstra īdṛśam /
na kāryaṃ patatāṃ hastālambaḥ sahyo na pātanam // 68
23.d:
स्वातन्त्र्यमात्रज्ञप्त्यै तु कथितं शास्त्र ईदृशम् ।
न कार्यं पततां हस्तालम्बः सह्यो न पातनम् ॥ 68
23.m: Such a thing is spoken of in scripture solely to make known absolute autonomy (svātantrya): / “Support with the hand is not to be given to those who are falling, [yet] their throwing down is not to be tolerated.”

23.s:
ata eva svatantratvādicchāyāḥ punarunmukham /
prāyaścittairviśodhyainaṃ dīkṣeta kṛpayā guruḥ // 69
23.d:
अत एव स्वतन्त्रत्वादिच्छायाः पुनरुन्मुखम् ।
प्रायश्चित्तैर्विशोध्यैनं दीक्षेत कृपया गुरुः ॥ 69
23.m: For this very reason, because of the autonomy of desire, the guru out of compassion should initiate him / when he turns back toward it, having purified him through expiations.

23.s:
ūrdhvadṛṣṭau prapannaḥ sannanāśvastastataḥ param /
adhaḥśāstraṃ prapadyāpi na śreyaḥpātratāmiyāt // 70
23.d:
ऊर्ध्वदृष्टौ प्रपन्नः सन्ननाश्वस्तस्ततः परम् ।
अधःशास्त्रं प्रपद्यापि न श्रेयःपात्रतामियात् ॥ 70
23.m: Having taken refuge in the higher view, if one subsequently loses faith, / even upon resorting to an inferior scripture he will not become a vessel of spiritual welfare.

23.s:
adhodṛṣṭau prapannastu tadanāśvastamānasaḥ /
ūrdhvaśāsanabhāk pāpaṃ taccojjhecca śivībhavet // 71
23.d:
अधोदृष्टौ प्रपन्नस्तु तदनाश्वस्तमानसः ।
ऊर्ध्वशासनभाक् पापं तच्चोज्झेच्च शिवीभवेत् ॥ 71
23.m: Having taken refuge in an inferior view, however, with mind lacking faith in that, / if he embraces the higher teaching, he sheds that sin and becomes Śiva.

23.s:
rājñe druhyannamātyāṅgabhūto'pi hi vihanyate /
viparyayastu netyevamūrdhvāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ samāśrayet // 72
23.d:
राज्ञे द्रुह्यन्नमात्याङ्गभूतोऽपि हि विहन्यते ।
विपर्ययस्तु नेत्येवमूर्ध्वां दृष्टिं समाश्रयेत् ॥ 72
23.m: For even an official who turns against the king is destroyed, / but the reverse is not so; in this way one should take refuge in the higher view. // 72

23.s:
śrīpūrvaśāstre tenoktaṃ yāvattenaiva noddhṛtaḥ /
atra hyartho'yametāvatpūrvoktajñānavṛṃhitaḥ // 73
23.d:
श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे तेनोक्तं यावत्तेनैव नोद्धृतः ।
अत्र ह्यर्थोऽयमेतावत्पूर्वोक्तज्ञानवृंहितः ॥ 73
23.m: Therefore it is stated in the venerable Mālinīvijayottara: 'As long as he is not uplifted by that very one...' / For here this meaning is magnified by the knowledge previously declared: // 73

23.s:
gurustāvatsa evātra tacchabdenāvamṛśyate /
tādṛksvabhyastavijñānabhājordhvapadaśālinā // 74
23.d:
गुरुस्तावत्स एवात्र तच्छब्देनावमृश्यते ।
तादृक्स्वभ्यस्तविज्ञानभाजोर्ध्वपदशालिना ॥ 74
23.m: The guru alone is referred to here by the word 'that', / one who possesses such well-practiced higher knowledge and abides in the higher station. // 74

23.s:
anuddhṛtasya na śreya etadanyagurūddhṛteḥ /
ata evāmbujanmārkadṛṣṭānto'tra nirūpitaḥ // 75
23.d:
अनुद्धृतस्य न श्रेय एतदन्यगुरूद्धृतेः ।
अत एवाम्बुजन्मार्कदृष्टान्तोऽत्र निरूपितः ॥ 75
23.m: For one who is not uplifted [by him], there is no welfare through being uplifted by another guru. / Precisely for this reason the analogy of the lotus and the sun has been explained here: // 75

23.s:
trijagajjyotiṣo hyanyattejo'nyacca niśākṛtaḥ /
jñānamanyattrikaguroranyattvadharavartinām // 76
23.d:
त्रिजगज्ज्योतिषो ह्यन्यत्तेजोऽन्यच्च निशाकृतः ।
ज्ञानमन्यत्त्रिकगुरोरन्यत्त्वधरवर्तिनाम् ॥ 76
23.m: Different indeed is the radiance of the illuminator of the three worlds [the sun], and different is that of the maker of night [the moon]; / different is the knowledge of a Trika guru, and different is that of those who abide in lower levels. // 76

23.s:
ata eva purābhūtagurvabhāvo yadā tadā /
tadanyaṃ lakṣaṇopetamāśrayetpunarunmukhaḥ // 77
23.d:
अत एव पुराभूतगुर्वभावो यदा तदा ।
तदन्यं लक्षणोपेतमाश्रयेत्पुनरुन्मुखः ॥ 77
23.m: For this very reason, when there is an absence of a former guru, / one should then, turning again in search, take refuge in another endowed with the requisite characteristics. // 77

23.s:
sati tasmiṃstūnmukhaḥ sankasmājjahyādyadi sphuṭam /
syādanyatarago doṣo yo'dhikārāpaghātakaḥ // 78
23.d:
सति तस्मिंस्तून्मुखः सन्कस्माज्जह्याद्यदि स्फुटम् ।
स्यादन्यतरगो दोषो योऽधिकारापघातकः ॥ 78
23.m: Yet while he is present, why would one, turning away, abandon him, unless clearly / there were a flaw residing in one or the other that destroys his entitlement? // 78

23.s:
doṣaśceha na lokastho doṣatvena nirūpyate /
ajñānakhyāpanāyuktakhyāpanātmā tvasau mataḥ // 79
23.d:
दोषश्चेह न लोकस्थो दोषत्वेन निरूप्यते ।
अज्ञानख्यापनायुक्तख्यापनात्मा त्वसौ मतः ॥ 79
23.m: And here, a flaw is not defined as being worldly in nature; / rather, it is considered to consist of proclaiming ignorance or improper proclamation. // 79

23.s:
śiṣyasyāpi tathābhūtajñānānāśvastarūpatā /
mukhyo doṣastadanye hi doṣāstatprabhavā yataḥ // 80
23.d:
शिष्यस्यापि तथाभूतज्ञानानाश्वस्तरूपता ।
मुख्यो दोषस्तदन्ये हि दोषास्तत्प्रभवा यतः ॥ 80
23.m: For the disciple too, lack of confidence in such knowledge / is the primary flaw; for all other flaws arise from that. // 80

23.s:
na dhvastavyādhikaḥ ko hi bhiṣajaṃ bahu manyate /
asūyurnūnamadhvastavyādhiḥ svasthāyate balāt // 81
23.d:
न ध्वस्तव्याधिकः को हि भिषजं बहु मन्यते ।
असूयुर्नूनमध्वस्तव्याधिः स्वस्थायते बलात् ॥ 81
23.m: For what person who has not had his illness eradicated holds the physician in high esteem? / Envious indeed, his illness uneradicated, he forcefully acts as though healthy. // 81

23.s:
evaṃ jñānasamāśvastaḥ kiṃ kiṃ na gurave caret /
no cennūnamaviśvasto viśvasta iva tiṣṭhati // 82
23.d:
एवं ज्ञानसमाश्वस्तः किं किं न गुरवे चरेत् ।
नो चेन्नूनमविश्वस्तो विश्वस्त इव तिष्ठति ॥ 82
23.m: Thus, one who has confidence in knowledge—what would he not do for the guru? / Otherwise, though utterly lacking in trust, he merely remains as if trusting. // 82

23.s:
ajñānādaya evaite doṣā na laukikā guroḥ /
iti khyāpayituṃ proktaṃ mālinīvijayottare // 83
23.d:
अज्ञानादय एवैते दोषा न लौकिका गुरोः ।
इति ख्यापयितुं प्रोक्तं मालिनीविजयोत्तरे ॥ 83
23.m: It is to make known that only these [deficiencies]—ignorance and the like—are the guru's flaws, not worldly ones, / that it is said in the Mālinīvijayottara: // 83

23.s:
na tasyānveṣayedvṛttaṃ śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham /
sa eva tadvijānāti yuktaṃ cāyuktameva vā // 84
23.d:
न तस्यान्वेषयेद्वृत्तं शुभं वा यदि वाशुभम् ।
स एव तद्विजानाति युक्तं चायुक्तमेव वा ॥ 84
23.m: 'One should not scrutinize his conduct, whether good or bad; / he alone knows that, whether it be appropriate or inappropriate.' // 84

23.s:
akāryeṣu yadā saktaḥ prāṇadravyāpahāriṣu /
tadā nivāraṇīyo'sau praṇatena vipaścitā // 85
23.d:
अकार्येषु यदा सक्तः प्राणद्रव्यापहारिषु ।
तदा निवारणीयोऽसौ प्रणतेन विपश्चिता ॥ 85
23.m: When he is attached to wrongful acts that deprive others of life or property, / he should then be restrained by the wise [disciple] bowing in deference. // 85

23.s:
viśeṣaṇamakāryāṇāmuktābhiprāyameva yat /
tenātivāryamāṇo'pi yadyasau na nivartate // 86
23.d:
विशेषणमकार्याणामुक्ताभिप्रायमेव यत् ।
तेनातिवार्यमाणोऽपि यद्यसौ न निवर्तते ॥ 86
23.m: The qualification of wrongful acts has precisely the aforementioned intention. / If, even when being dissuaded by him, he does not desist, // 86

23.s:
tadānyatra kvacidgatvā śivamevānucintayet /
na hyasya sa gurutve syāddoṣo yenoṣare kṛṣim // 87
23.d:
तदान्यत्र क्वचिद्गत्वा शिवमेवानुचिन्तयेत् ।
न ह्यस्य स गुरुत्वे स्याद्दोषो येनोषरे कृषिम् ॥ 87
23.m: then, having gone elsewhere, one should contemplate Śiva alone. / For in him there would be no such flaw in guruhood by which one would cultivate barren soil // 87

23.s:
kuryādvrajenniśāyāṃ vā sa tvarthaprāṇahārakaḥ /
tadīyāpriyabhīrustu paraṃ tādṛśamācaret // 88
23.d:
कुर्याद्व्रजेन्निशायां वा स त्वर्थप्राणहारकः ।
तदीयाप्रियभीरुस्तु परं तादृशमाचरेत् ॥ 88
23.m: or walk into the night; rather, he is one who robs wealth and life. / But one who fears doing him an unpleasantness should behave in an exemplary manner towards him. // 88

23.s:
yatastadapriyaṃ naiṣa śṛṇuyāditi bhāṣitam /
śrīmātaṅge taduktaṃ ca nādhītaṃ bhūmabhītitaḥ // 89
23.d:
यतस्तदप्रियं नैष शृणुयादिति भाषितम् ।
श्रीमातङ्गे तदुक्तं च नाधीतं भूमभीतितः ॥ 89
23.m: For it has been stated: 'He should not hear what is unpleasant to him'; / and that has been stated in the venerable Mātaṅga, but it is not cited here for fear of prolixity. // 89

23.s:
yaccaitaduktametāvatkartavyamiti taddhruvam /
tīvraśaktigṛhītānāṃ svayameva hṛdi sphuret // 90
23.d:
यच्चैतदुक्तमेतावत्कर्तव्यमिति तद्ध्रुवम् ।
तीव्रशक्तिगृहीतानां स्वयमेव हृदि स्फुरेत् ॥ 90
23.m: And as for this which has been stated, that this much is to be done—surely / this flashes forth spontaneously in the heart of those seized by intense power. // 90

23.s:
upadeśastvayaṃ mandamadhyaśakternijāṃ kramāt /
śaktiṃ jvalayituṃ proktaḥ sā hyevaṃ jājvalītyalam // 91
23.d:
उपदेशस्त्वयं मन्दमध्यशक्तेर्निजां क्रमात् ।
शक्तिं ज्वलयितुं प्रोक्तः सा ह्येवं जाज्वलीत्यलम् ॥ 91
23.m: This instruction, however, has been taught in order gradually to ignite their own power / in those of dull or middling power; for thus it blazes forth abundantly. // 91

23.s:
dṛḍhānurāgasubhagasaṃrambhābhogabhāginaḥ /
svollāsi smarasarvasyaṃ dārḍhyāyānyatra dṛśyate // 92
23.d:
दृढानुरागसुभगसंरम्भाभोगभागिनः ।
स्वोल्लासि स्मरसर्वस्यं दार्ढ्यायान्यत्र दृश्यते ॥ 92
23.m: For one who possesses the expanse of intense passion and charming eagerness, / the totality of desire, flashing of its own accord, is seen elsewhere for the sake of confirmation. // 92

23.s:
nanveṣa kasmāddṛṣṭāntaḥ kimetenāśubhaṃ kṛtam /
citspandaḥ sarvago bhinnādupādheḥ sa tathā tathā // 93
23.d:
नन्वेष कस्माद्दृष्टान्तः किमेतेनाशुभं कृतम् ।
चित्स्पन्दः सर्वगो भिन्नादुपाधेः स तथा तथा ॥ 93
23.m: Indeed, why this example? Has anything inauspicious been caused by it? / The pulsation of consciousness is omnipresent; through varying conditions it becomes this and that: // 93

23.s:
bhavetko'pi tirobhūtaḥ punarunmukhito'pi san /
vināpi daiśikātprāgvatsvayameva vimucyate // 94
23.d:
भवेत्कोऽपि तिरोभूतः पुनरुन्मुखितोऽपि सन् ।
विनापि दैशिकात्प्राग्वत्स्वयमेव विमुच्यते ॥ 94
23.m: Someone, even while concealed, turns upward again / and is liberated spontaneously, just as before, even without a guru. // 94

23.s:
prakārastveṣa nātroktaḥ śaktipātabalādgataḥ /
asaṃbhāvyatayā cātra dṛḍhakopaprasādavat // 95
23.d:
प्रकारस्त्वेष नात्रोक्तः शक्तिपातबलाद्गतः ।
असंभाव्यतया चात्र दृढकोपप्रसादवत् ॥ 95
23.m: This modality, however, is not explained here, as it is attained through the power of the descent of power / and because of its improbability here, like deep anger and favor. // 95

23.s:
ityeṣa yo guroḥ prokto vidhistaṃ pālayedguruḥ /
anyathā na śivaṃ yāyācchrīmatsāre ca varṇitam // 96
23.d:
इत्येष यो गुरोः प्रोक्तो विधिस्तं पालयेद्गुरुः ।
अन्यथा न शिवं यायाच्छ्रीमत्सारे च वर्णितम् ॥ 96
23.m: Thus, the guru should maintain this rule that has been stated for the guru; / otherwise he would not attain to Śiva. And it is described in the venerable Sāra: // 96

23.s:
anyāyaṃ ye prakurvanti śāstrārthaṃ varjayantyalam /
te'rdhanārīśapuragā guravaḥ samayacyutāḥ // 97
23.d:
अन्यायं ये प्रकुर्वन्ति शास्त्रार्थं वर्जयन्त्यलम् ।
तेऽर्धनारीशपुरगा गुरवः समयच्युताः ॥ 97
23.m: 'Those who commit injustice and completely abandon the scriptural meaning— / those gurus, fallen from the rule, go to the city of Ardhanārīśa.' // 97

23.s:
anyatrāpyadhikāraṃ ca neyādvidyeśatāṃ vrajet /
anyatra samayatyāgātkravyādatvaṃ śataṃ samāḥ // 98
23.d:
अन्यत्राप्यधिकारं च नेयाद्विद्येशतां व्रजेत् ।
अन्यत्र समयत्यागात्क्रव्यादत्वं शतं समाः ॥ 98
23.m: Elsewhere too, it is taught that he would not attain authority, but would become a lord of knowledge; / elsewhere, that because of abandoning the rule he becomes a flesh-eater for a hundred years. // 98

23.s:
iyattatratyatātparyaṃ siddhāntagururunnayaḥ /
bhavetpiśācavidyeśaḥ śuddha eva tu tāntrikaḥ // 99
23.d:
इयत्तत्रत्यतात्पर्यं सिद्धान्तगुरुरुन्नयः ।
भवेत्पिशाचविद्येशः शुद्ध एव तु तान्त्रिकः ॥ 99
23.m: This is the underlying meaning of that [text]: a Siddhānta guru would be elevated / to become a piśāca and a lord of knowledge, while a purely Tantric guru // 99

23.s:
ṣaḍardhadaiśikaścārdhanārīśabhuvanasthitiḥ /
eṣā karmapradhānānāṃ gurūṇāṃ gatirucyate // 100
23.d:
षडर्धदैशिकश्चार्धनारीशभुवनस्थितिः ।
एषा कर्मप्रधानानां गुरूणां गतिरुच्यते ॥ 100
23.m: and a Trika teacher would abide in the realm of Ardhanārīśa. / This is declared to be the destiny of gurus for whom ritual action is primary. // 100

23.s:
jñānināṃ caiṣa no bandha iti sarvatra varṇitam /
sādhakasyābhiṣeke'pi sarvo'yaṃ kathyate vidhiḥ // 101
23.d:
ज्ञानिनां चैष नो बन्ध इति सर्वत्र वर्णितम् ।
साधकस्याभिषेकेऽपि सर्वोऽयं कथ्यते विधिः ॥ 101
23.m: And it is everywhere described that this bondage does not apply to the knowers. / All this procedure is also stated in the consecration of the adept: // 101

23.s:
adhikārārpaṇaṃ nātra naca vidyāvrataṃ kila /
sādhyamantrārpaṇaṃ tvatra svopayogikriyākrame // 102
23.d:
अधिकारार्पणं नात्र नच विद्याव्रतं किल ।
साध्यमन्त्रार्पणं त्वत्र स्वोपयोगिक्रियाक्रमे ॥ 102
23.m: There is no conferral of authority here, nor indeed the vow of the Vidyā; / rather, here is the conferral of the mantra to be mastered, in the sequence of actions useful to oneself. // 102

23.s:
samaste'pyupadeśaḥ syānnijopakaraṇārpaṇam /
abhiṣekavidhirnirūpitaḥ parameśena yathā nirūpitaḥ // 103
23.d:
समस्तेऽप्युपदेशः स्यान्निजोपकरणार्पणम् ।
अभिषेकविधिर्निरूपितः परमेशेन यथा निरूपितः ॥ 103
23.m: There should be instruction in everything, and the handing over of one's own implements. / The procedure of consecration has been explained as it was taught by the Supreme Lord. // 103

24.s: atha śāmbhavaśāsanoditāṃ sarahasyāṃ śṛṇutāntyasaṃskriyām // 1
24.d: अथ शाम्भवशासनोदितां सरहस्यां शृणुतान्त्यसंस्क्रियाम् ॥ 1
24.m: Now listen to the secret final sacrament proclaimed in the Śāmbhava teaching: // 1b

24.s:
sarveṣāmadharasthānāṃ gurvantānāmapi sphuṭam /
śaktipātātpurāproktātkuryādantyeṣṭidīkṣaṇam // 2
24.d:
सर्वेषामधरस्थानां गुर्वन्तानामपि स्फुटम् ।
शक्तिपातात्पुराप्रोक्तात्कुर्यादन्त्येष्टिदीक्षणम् ॥ 2
24.m: For all who reside in lower stages, up to and including the gurus, / one should perform the funeral initiation clearly through the descent of power previously explained. // 2

24.s:
ūrdhvaśāsanagānāṃ ca samayopahatātmanām /
antyeṣṭidīkṣā kartavyā guruṇā tattvavedinā // 3
24.d:
ऊर्ध्वशासनगानां च समयोपहतात्मनाम् ।
अन्त्येष्टिदीक्षा कर्तव्या गुरुणा तत्त्ववेदिना ॥ 3
24.m: And for those belonging to higher teachings whose nature has been ruined by [breach of] the rule, / the funeral initiation must be performed by a guru who knows reality. // 3

24.s:
samayācāradoṣeṣu pramādātskhalitasya hi /
antyeṣṭidīkṣā kāryeti śrīdīkṣottaraśāsane // 4
24.d:
समयाचारदोषेषु प्रमादात्स्खलितस्य हि ।
अन्त्येष्टिदीक्षा कार्येति श्रीदीक्षोत्तरशासने ॥ 4
24.m: For in the venerable Dīkṣottara teaching [it is said] that the funeral initiation is to be performed / for one who has stumbled inadvertently into faults regarding the conduct of the rule. // 4

24.s:
yatkiṃcitkathitaṃ pūrvaṃ mṛtoddhārābhidhe vidhau /
pratimāyāṃ tadevātra sarvaṃ śavatanau caret // 5
24.d:
यत्किंचित्कथितं पूर्वं मृतोद्धाराभिधे विधौ ।
प्रतिमायां तदेवात्र सर्वं शवतनौ चरेत् ॥ 5
24.m: Whatever was described earlier in the procedure called the uplifting of the dead / on an image, all of that should be performed here on the corpse's body. // 5

24.s:
śrīsiddhātantrakathito vidhireṣa nirūpyate /
antimaṃ yadbhavetpūrvaṃ tatkṛtvāntimamādimam // 6
24.d:
श्रीसिद्धातन्त्रकथितो विधिरेष निरूप्यते ।
अन्तिमं यद्भवेत्पूर्वं तत्कृत्वान्तिममादिमम् ॥ 6
24.m: This procedure described in the venerable Siddhātantra is now explained: / having made whatever is last first, and the last first, // 6

24.s:
saṃhṛtyaikaikamiṣṭiryā sāntyeṣṭirdvitayī matā /
pūjādhyānajapāpluṣṭasamaye natu sādhake // 7
24.d:
संहृत्यैकैकमिष्टिर्या सान्त्येष्टिर्द्वितयी मता ।
पूजाध्यानजपाप्लुष्टसमये नतु साधके ॥ 7
24.m: the sacrifice which dissolves each one by one is considered a twofold funeral rite. / But for an adept whose rule has been consumed by worship, meditation, and recitation, // 7

24.s:
piṇḍapātādayaṃ muktaḥ khecaro vā bhavetpriye /
ācārye tattvasaṃpanne yatra tatra mṛte sati // 8
24.d:
पिण्डपातादयं मुक्तः खेचरो वा भवेत्प्रिये ।
आचार्ये तत्त्वसंपन्ने यत्र तत्र मृते सति ॥ 8
24.m: upon the fall of the body, O beloved, he becomes liberated or moves through the skies. / When a master endowed with reality dies anywhere whatsoever, // 8

24.s:
antyeṣṭirnaiva vidyeta śuddhacetasyamūrdhani /
mantrayogādibhirye ca māritā narake tu te // 9
24.d:
अन्त्येष्टिर्नैव विद्येत शुद्धचेतस्यमूर्धनि ।
मन्त्रयोगादिभिर्ये च मारिता नरके तु ते ॥ 9
24.m: no funeral rite at all exists for him whose consciousness is pure, without crown-aperture [obstruction]. / And those who have been killed through mantra-sorcery and the like are in hell; // 9

24.s:
kāryā teṣāmihāntyeṣṭirguruṇātikṛpālunā /
na maṇḍalādikaṃ tvatra bhavecchamāśānike vidhau // 10
24.d:
कार्या तेषामिहान्त्येष्टिर्गुरुणातिकृपालुना ।
न मण्डलादिकं त्वत्र भवेच्छमाशानिके विधौ ॥ 10
24.m: for them, the funeral rite must be performed here by a deeply compassionate guru. / However, there should be no maṇḍala or the like here in the cremation-ground rite. // 10

24.s:
kecittadapi kartavyamūcire pretasadmani /
pūjayitvā vibhuṃ sarvaṃ nyāsaṃ pūrvavadācaret // 11
24.d:
केचित्तदपि कर्तव्यमूचिरे प्रेतसद्मनि ।
पूजयित्वा विभुं सर्वं न्यासं पूर्ववदाचरेत् ॥ 11
24.m: Some have declared that even that should be performed in the abode of the dead; / having worshipped the All-pervading Lord, one should perform the entire imposition as before. // 11

24.s:
saṃhārakramayogena caraṇānmūrdhapaścimam /
tathaiva bodhayedenaṃ kriyājñānasamādhibhiḥ // 12
24.d:
संहारक्रमयोगेन चरणान्मूर्धपश्चिमम् ।
तथैव बोधयेदेनं क्रियाज्ञानसमाधिभिः ॥ 12
24.m: Through the method of the sequence of dissolution, from the feet to the top of the head, / one should awaken him in the same manner through action, knowledge, and absorption. // 12

24.s:
bindunā rodhayettattvaṃ śaktibījena vedhayet /
ghaṭṭayennādadeśe tu triśūlena tu tāḍayet // 13
24.d:
बिन्दुना रोधयेत्तत्त्वं शक्तिबीजेन वेधयेत् ।
घट्टयेन्नाददेशे तु त्रिशूलेन तु ताडयेत् ॥ 13
24.m: One should obstruct the reality with the point, pierce it with the seed-syllable of power, / agitate it in the region of the resonance, and strike it with the trident. // 13

24.s:
suṣumnāntargatenaiva visargeṇa punaḥ punaḥ /
tāḍayeta kalāḥ sarvāḥ kampate'sau tataḥ paśuḥ // 14
24.d:
सुषुम्नान्तर्गतेनैव विसर्गेण पुनः पुनः ।
ताडयेत कलाः सर्वाः कम्पतेऽसौ ततः पशुः ॥ 14
24.m:
With the creative emission situated within the suṣumnā itself, he should strike
all the parts again and again; then that bound soul trembles.

24.s:
utkṣipedvāmahastaṃ vā tatastaṃ yojayetpare /
pratyayena vinā mokṣo hyaśraddheyo vimohitaiḥ // 15
24.d:
उत्क्षिपेद्वामहस्तं वा ततस्तं योजयेत्परे ।
प्रत्ययेन विना मोक्षो ह्यश्रद्धेयो विमोहितैः ॥ 15
24.m:
Or he should raise his left hand, and then unite him with the Supreme;
for without tangible proof, liberation is not believed by those who are deluded.

24.s:
tadarthametaduditaṃ natu mokṣopayogyadaḥ /
ityūce parameśaḥ śrīkulagahvaraśāsane // 16
24.d:
तदर्थमेतदुदितं नतु मोक्षोपयोग्यदः ।
इत्यूचे परमेशः श्रीकुलगह्वरशासने ॥ 16
24.m:
It is for this purpose that this was taught, not that this [trembling] produces liberation—
thus spoke the Supreme Lord in the scripture of the venerable Kulagahvara.

24.s:
sādhyo'numeyo mokṣādiḥ pratyayairyadatīndriyaḥ /
dīkṣottare ca puryaṣṭavargārpaṇamihoditam // 17
24.d:
साध्योऽनुमेयो मोक्षादिः प्रत्ययैर्यदतीन्द्रियः ।
दीक्षोत्तरे च पुर्यष्टवर्गार्पणमिहोदितम् ॥ 17
24.m:
Since liberation and the like are imperceptible by the senses, they are to be proved and inferred by tangible signs.
And in the Dīkṣottara, the offering of the set of the subtle body is taught here.

24.s:
tadvidhiḥ śrutipatre'bje madhye devaṃ sadāśivam /
īśarudraharibrahmacatuṣkaṃ prāgdigāditaḥ // 18
24.d:
तद्विधिः श्रुतिपत्रेऽब्जे मध्ये देवं सदाशिवम् ।
ईशरुद्रहरिब्रह्मचतुष्कं प्राग्दिगादितः ॥ 18
24.m:
The procedure for that: on a four-petalled lotus, having worshipped Lord Sadāśiva in the center
and the quartet of Īśa, Rudra, Hari, and Brahmā starting from the east and so on,

24.s:
pūjayitvā śrutisparśau rasaṃ gandhaṃ vapurdvayam /
dhyahaṃkṛtī manaśceti brahmādiṣvarpayetkramāt // 19
24.d:
पूजयित्वा श्रुतिस्पर्शौ रसं गन्धं वपुर्द्वयम् ।
ध्यहंकृती मनश्चेति ब्रह्मादिष्वर्पयेत्क्रमात् ॥ 19
24.m:
and having worshipped hearing and touch, taste, smell, both forms of the physical body,
intellect, egoity, and the mind, he should offer them successively to Brahmā and the others.

24.s:
eteṣāṃ tarpaṇaṃ kṛtvā śatahomena daiśikaḥ /
eṣā sāṃnyāsikī dīkṣā puryaṣṭakaviśodhanī // 20
24.d:
एतेषां तर्पणं कृत्वा शतहोमेन दैशिकः ।
एषा सांन्यासिकी दीक्षा पुर्यष्टकविशोधनी ॥ 20
24.m:
Having performed their satisfaction with a hundred oblations, the guide [concludes it];
this is the renouncer's initiation, which purifies the subtle body.

24.s:
puryaṣṭakasyābhāve ca na svarganarakādayaḥ /
tathā kṛtvā na kartavyaṃ laukikaṃ kiṃcanāpi hi // 21
24.d:
पुर्यष्टकस्याभावे च न स्वर्गनरकादयः ।
तथा कृत्वा न कर्तव्यं लौकिकं किंचनापि हि ॥ 21
24.m:
And in the absence of the subtle body, heaven, hell, and the like do not exist.
Having performed this, no worldly rite whatsoever should be performed.

24.s:
uktaṃ śrīmādhavakule śāsanastho mṛteṣvapi /
piṇḍapātodakāsrvādi laukikaṃ parivarjayet // 22
24.d:
उक्तं श्रीमाधवकुले शासनस्थो मृतेष्वपि ।
पिण्डपातोदकास्र्वादि लौकिकं परिवर्जयेत् ॥ 22
24.m:
It is stated in the venerable Mādhavakula: one who abides by the teaching, even when someone has died,
should avoid worldly rites such as the offering of rice-balls, libation water, and blood.

24.s:
śivaṃ saṃpūjya cakrārcāṃ yathāśakti samācaret /
kramāttridaśamatriṃśatriṃśavatsaravāsare // 23
24.d:
शिवं संपूज्य चक्रार्चां यथाशक्ति समाचरेत् ।
क्रमात्त्रिदशमत्रिंशत्रिंशवत्सरवासरे ॥ 23
24.m:
Having worshipped Śiva, he should perform the worship of the circle according to his capacity
in succession on the third day, the tenth day, the thirtieth day, and on the day of the year.

24.s: ityukto'ntyeṣṭiyāgo'yaṃ parameśvarabhāṣitaḥ // 24
24.d: इत्युक्तोऽन्त्येष्टियागोऽयं परमेश्वरभाषितः ॥ 24
24.m: Thus has been taught this sacrifice of the funeral rite declared by the Supreme Lord.

25.s: atha śrāddhavidhiḥ śrīmatṣaḍardhokto nigadyate // 1
25.d: अथ श्राद्धविधिः श्रीमत्षडर्धोक्तो निगद्यते ॥ 1
25.m: Now the procedure for the post-funerary rites taught in the venerable Trika is expounded.

25.s:
siddhātantre sūcito'sau mūrtiyāganirūpaṇe /
antyeṣṭyā suviśuddhānāmaśuddhānāṃ ca tadvidhiḥ // 2
25.d:
सिद्धातन्त्रे सूचितोऽसौ मूर्तियागनिरूपणे ।
अन्त्येष्ट्या सुविशुद्धानामशुद्धानां च तद्विधिः ॥ 2
25.m:
This was indicated in the Siddhātantra in the exposition of the sacrifice of the divine form;
and that procedure is for those who are purified by the funeral rite and for those who are unpurified.

25.s:
tryahe turye'hni daśame māsi māsyādyavatsare /
varṣe varṣe sarvakālaṃ kāryastatsvaiḥ sa pūrvavat // 3
25.d:
त्र्यहे तुर्येऽह्नि दशमे मासि मास्याद्यवत्सरे ।
वर्षे वर्षे सर्वकालं कार्यस्तत्स्वैः स पूर्ववत् ॥ 3
25.m:
On the third day, on the fourth day, on the tenth, month by month, in the first year,
and every year at all times, it is to be performed by his kin as before.

25.s:
tatra prāgvadyajeddevaṃ homayedanale tathā /
tato naivedyameva prāggṛhītvā hastagocare // 4
25.d:
तत्र प्राग्वद्यजेद्देवं होमयेदनले तथा ।
ततो नैवेद्यमेव प्राग्गृहीत्वा हस्तगोचरे ॥ 4
25.m:
There, as before, he should worship the deity and likewise make oblation into the fire;
then, having first taken the food offering into the range of his hands,

25.s:
gururannamayīṃ śaktiṃ vṛṃhikāṃ vīryarūpiṇīm /
dhyātvā tayā samāviṣṭaṃ taṃ sādhyaṃ cintayetsudhīḥ // 5
25.d:
गुरुरन्नमयीं शक्तिं वृंहिकां वीर्यरूपिणीम् ।
ध्यात्वा तया समाविष्टं तं साध्यं चिन्तयेत्सुधीः ॥ 5
25.m:
the guru, meditating upon the expanding power consisting of food and having the nature of virility,
wise in mind, should contemplate the beneficiary as pervaded by it.

25.s:
tato'sya yaḥ pāśavo'ṃśo bhogyarūpastamarpayet /
bhoktaryekātmabhāvena śiṣya itthaṃ śivībhavet // 6
25.d:
ततोऽस्य यः पाशवोऽंशो भोग्यरूपस्तमर्पयेत् ।
भोक्तर्येकात्मभावेन शिष्य इत्थं शिवीभवेत् ॥ 6
25.m:
Then, whatever is his bound portion having the nature of the object of enjoyment, he should offer it
into the enjoyer with a sense of identity; in this way the disciple becomes Śiva.

25.s:
bhogyatānyā tanurdeha iti pāśātmakā matāḥ /
śrāddhe mṛtoddhṛtāvantayāge teṣāṃ śivīkṛtiḥ // 7
25.d:
भोग्यतान्या तनुर्देह इति पाशात्मका मताः ।
श्राद्धे मृतोद्धृतावन्तयागे तेषां शिवीकृतिः ॥ 7
25.m:
The other nature of being an object of enjoyment, the subtle body and the physical body, are held to consist of bondage;
in the post-funerary rite, in the liberation of the deceased, and in the final sacrifice, they are transformed into Śiva.

25.s:
ekenaiva vidhānena yadyapi syātkṛtārthatā /
tathāpi tanmayībhāvasiddhyai sarvaṃ vidhiṃ caret // 8
25.d:
एकेनैव विधानेन यद्यपि स्यात्कृतार्थता ।
तथापि तन्मयीभावसिद्ध्यै सर्वं विधिं चरेत् ॥ 8
25.m:
Even though fulfillment may come through a single rite alone,
nevertheless, for the accomplishment of identity with That, he should perform the entire ritual.

25.s:
bubhukṣostu kriyābhyāsabhūmānau phalabhūmani /
hetu tato mṛtoddhāraśrāddhādyasmai samācaret // 9
25.d:
बुभुक्षोस्तु क्रियाभ्यासभूमानौ फलभूमनि ।
हेतु ततो मृतोद्धारश्राद्धाद्यस्मै समाचरेत् ॥ 9
25.m:
For one who desires enjoyment, an abundance of ritual practice leads to an abundance of fruit;
therefore, for him, he should perform the liberation of the dead, the post-funerary rites, and the like.

25.s:
tattvajñānārkavidhvastadhvāntasya tu na ko'pyayam /
antyeṣṭiśrāddhavidhyādirupayogī kadācana // 10
25.d:
तत्त्वज्ञानार्कविध्वस्तध्वान्तस्य तु न कोऽप्ययम् ।
अन्त्येष्टिश्राद्धविध्यादिरुपयोगी कदाचन ॥ 10
25.m:
For one whose darkness has been destroyed by the sun of the knowledge of reality, however,
no such procedure of funeral rites, post-funerary rites, and the like is ever of any use.

25.s:
teṣāṃ tu guru tadvargavargyasabrahmacāriṇām /
tatsantānajuṣāmaikyadinaṃ parvadinaṃ bhavet // 11
25.d:
तेषां तु गुरु तद्वर्गवर्ग्यसब्रह्मचारिणाम् ।
तत्सन्तानजुषामैक्यदिनं पर्वदिनं भवेत् ॥ 11
25.m:
For them, however, of the guru, his peers, his fellow students,
and those who belong to that lineage, the day of unification becomes a festive day.

25.s:
yadāhi bodhasyodrekastadā parvāha pūraṇāt /
janmaikyadivasau tena parvaṇī bodhasiddhitaḥ // 12
25.d:
यदाहि बोधस्योद्रेकस्तदा पर्वाह पूरणात् ।
जन्मैक्यदिवसौ तेन पर्वणी बोधसिद्धितः ॥ 12
25.m:
For when consciousness overflows, that is called a festival because of fullness;
therefore, the day of birth and the day of unification are both festive days due to the attainment of consciousness.

25.s:
putrako'pi yadā kasmaicana syādupakārakaḥ /
tadā mātuḥ pituḥ śaktervāmadakṣāntarālagāḥ // 13
25.d:
पुत्रकोऽपि यदा कस्मैचन स्यादुपकारकः ।
तदा मातुः पितुः शक्तेर्वामदक्षान्तरालगाः ॥ 13
25.m:
Even when a spiritual son does not serve any [purpose],
then, moving between the left and right power of the mother and father,

25.s:
nāḍīḥ pravāhayeddevāyārpayeta niveditam /
śrīmadbharuṇatantre ca tacchivena nirūpitam // 14
25.d:
नाडीः प्रवाहयेद्देवायार्पयेत निवेदितम् ।
श्रीमद्भरुणतन्त्रे च तच्छिवेन निरूपितम् ॥ 14
25.m:
he should cause the channels to flow and offer what has been dedicated to the deity;
and in the venerable Bharuṇatantra, that has been explained by Śiva.

25.s:
tadvāhakālāpekṣā ca kāryā tadrūpasiddhaye /
svācchandyenātha tatsiddhiṃ vidhinā bhāvinā caret // 15
25.d:
तद्वाहकालापेक्षा च कार्या तद्रूपसिद्धये ।
स्वाच्छन्द्येनाथ तत्सिद्धिं विधिना भाविना चरेत् ॥ 15
25.m:
And regard should be paid to the time of their flowing for the attainment of that state;
or according to his free will he should perform that accomplishment by the procedure that follows.

25.s:
yasya kasyāpi vā śrāddhe gurudevāgnitarpaṇam /
sacakreṣṭi bhavecchrauto natu syātpāśavo vidhiḥ // 16
25.d:
यस्य कस्यापि वा श्राद्धे गुरुदेवाग्नितर्पणम् ।
सचक्रेष्टि भवेच्छ्रौतो नतु स्यात्पाशवो विधिः ॥ 16
25.m:
In the post-funerary rite of anyone whatsoever, the satisfaction of the guru, the deity, and the fire,
together with the sacrifice of the circle, is scriptural, but the rite for the bound soul should not be performed.

25.s:
śrīmaukuṭe tathā coktaṃ śivaśāstre sthito'pi yaḥ /
pratyeti vaidike bhagnaghaṇṭāvanna sa kiṃcana // 17
25.d:
श्रीमौकुटे तथा चोक्तं शिवशास्त्रे स्थितोऽपि यः ।
प्रत्येति वैदिके भग्नघण्टावन्न स किंचन ॥ 17
25.m:
And likewise it is said in the venerable Maukuṭa: he who, though abiding in the Śaiva teaching,
believes in the Vedic rite, is like a cracked bell—he is nothing at all.

25.s:
tathoktadevapūjādicakrayāgāntakarmaṇā /
rudratvametyasau janturbhogāndivyānsamaśnute // 18
25.d:
तथोक्तदेवपूजादिचक्रयागान्तकर्मणा ।
रुद्रत्वमेत्यसौ जन्तुर्भोगान्दिव्यान्समश्नुते ॥ 18
25.m:
By the ritual thus described, ending with the worship of the deity and the sacrifice of the circle,
this creature attains Rudrahood and experiences divine enjoyments.

25.s:
atha vacmaḥ sphuṭaṃ śrīmatsiddhaye nāḍicāraṇam /
yā vāhayitumiṣyeta nāḍī tāmeva bhāvayet // 19
25.d:
अथ वच्मः स्फुटं श्रीमत्सिद्धये नाडिचारणम् ।
या वाहयितुमिष्येत नाडी तामेव भावयेत् ॥ 19
25.m:
Now we clearly explain the activation of the channels for the sacred accomplishment:
whichever channel one wishes to make flow, one should contemplate precisely that one.

25.s:
bhāvanātanmayībhāve sā nāḍī vahati sphuṭam /
yadvā vāhayituṃ yeṣṭā tadaṅgaṃ tena pāṇinā // 20
25.d:
भावनातन्मयीभावे सा नाडी वहति स्फुटम् ।
यद्वा वाहयितुं येष्टा तदङ्गं तेन पाणिना ॥ 20
25.m:
When there is identity through contemplation, that channel clearly flows;
or whichever one wishes to make flow, by pressing that limb with that hand

25.s:
āpīḍya kukṣiṃ namayetsā vahennāḍikā kṣaṇāt /
evaṃ śrāddhamukhenāpi bhogamokṣobhayasthitim // 21
25.d:
आपीड्य कुक्षिं नमयेत्सा वहेन्नाडिका क्षणात् ।
एवं श्राद्धमुखेनापि भोगमोक्षोभयस्थितिम् ॥ 21
25.m:
and bending the belly, that channel flows in an instant.
Thus, even through the means of the post-funerary rite, the state of both enjoyment and liberation

25.s:
kuryāditi śivenoktaṃ tatra tatra kṛpālunā /
śaktipātodaye jantoryenopāyena daiśikaḥ // 22
25.d:
कुर्यादिति शिवेनोक्तं तत्र तत्र कृपालुना ।
शक्तिपातोदये जन्तोर्येनोपायेन दैशिकः ॥ 22
25.m:
should be brought about; thus it has been stated here and there by the compassionate Śiva.
Upon the arising of the descent of power in a creature, by whatever means the guide

25.s:
karotyuddharaṇaṃ tattannirvāṇāyāsya kalpate /
uddhartā devadevo hi sa cācintyaprabhāvakaḥ // 23
25.d:
करोत्युद्धरणं तत्तन्निर्वाणायास्य कल्पते ।
उद्धर्ता देवदेवो हि स चाचिन्त्यप्रभावकः ॥ 23
25.m:
effects his elevation, that very means suffices for his liberation;
for the uplifter is the God of gods, and his power is unthinkable.

25.s:
upāyaṃ gurudīkṣādidvāramātreṇa saṃśrayet /
uktaṃ śrīmanmataṅgākhye munipraśnādanantaram // 24
25.d:
उपायं गुरुदीक्षादिद्वारमात्रेण संश्रयेत् ।
उक्तं श्रीमन्मतङ्गाख्ये मुनिप्रश्नादनन्तरम् ॥ 24
25.m:
He should resort to the means solely through the door of the guru, initiation, and the like.
It is said in the venerable work named Mataṅga after the sage's question:

25.s:
muktirvivekāttattvānāṃ dīkṣāto yogato yadi /
caryāmātrātkathaṃ sā syādityataḥ samamuttaram // 25
25.d:
मुक्तिर्विवेकात्तत्त्वानां दीक्षातो योगतो यदि ।
चर्यामात्रात्कथं सा स्यादित्यतः सममुत्तरम् ॥ 25
25.m:
'If liberation is through discernment of the reality levels, through initiation, and through yoga,
how can it occur through mere conduct?' To this there is an appropriate reply:

25.s:
prahasyoce vibhuḥ kasmādbhrāntiste parameśituḥ /
sarvānugrāhakatvaṃ hi saṃsiddhaṃ dṛśyatāṃ kila // 26
25.d:
प्रहस्योचे विभुः कस्माद्भ्रान्तिस्ते परमेशितुः ।
सर्वानुग्राहकत्वं हि संसिद्धं दृश्यतां किल ॥ 26
25.m:
Smiling, the omnipresent Lord said: 'Why is there delusion in you?
Indeed, look! The fact that the Supreme Lord bestows grace on all is well established.

25.s:
prāptamṛtyorviṣavyādhiśastrādi kila kāraṇam /
alpaṃ vā bahu vā tadvadanudhyā muktikāraṇam // 27
25.d:
प्राप्तमृत्योर्विषव्याधिशस्त्रादि किल कारणम् ।
अल्पं वा बहु वा तद्वदनुध्या मुक्तिकारणम् ॥ 27
25.m:
For one whose death has come, poison, disease, weapons, and so forth are indeed the cause,
whether slight or great; similarly, contemplation is the cause of liberation.

25.s:
muktyarthamupacaryante bāhyaliṅgānyamūni tu /
iti jñātvā na sandeha itthaṃ kāryo vipaścitā // 28
25.d:
मुक्त्यर्थमुपचर्यन्ते बाह्यलिङ्गान्यमूनि तु ।
इति ज्ञात्वा न सन्देह इत्थं कार्यो विपश्चिता ॥ 28
25.m:
These external marks, however, are applied only for the purpose of liberation.'
Knowing this, no doubt of this kind should be harbored by the wise:

25.s:
iyataiva kathaṃ muktiriti bhaktiṃ parāṃ śrayet /
uktaḥ śrāddhavidhirbhrāntigarātaṅkavimardanaḥ // 29
25.d:
इयतैव कथं मुक्तिरिति भक्तिं परां श्रयेत् ।
उक्तः श्राद्धविधिर्भ्रान्तिगरातङ्कविमर्दनः ॥ 29
25.m:
'How could liberation come through just this much?' He should resort to supreme devotion.
The procedure of post-funerary rites, which crushes the terrible fear of delusion, has been declared.

26.s: athocyate śeṣavṛttirjīvatāmupayoginī // 1
26.d: अथोच्यते शेषवृत्तिर्जीवतामुपयोगिनी ॥ 1
26.m: Now is taught the remaining course of conduct useful for the living.

26.s:
dīkṣā bahuprakāreyaṃ śrāddhāntā yā prakīrtitā /
sā saṃskriyāyai mokṣāya bhogāyāpi dvayāya vā // 2
26.d:
दीक्षा बहुप्रकारेयं श्राद्धान्ता या प्रकीर्तिता ।
सा संस्क्रियायै मोक्षाय भोगायापि द्वयाय वा ॥ 2
26.m:
This initiation of many kinds, ending with the post-funerary rites, which has been proclaimed—
it is for consecration, for liberation, or also for enjoyment, or for both.

26.s:
tatra saṃskārasiddhyai yā dīkṣā sākṣānna mocanī /
anusaṃdhivaśādyā ca sākṣānmoktrī sabījikā // 3
26.d:
तत्र संस्कारसिद्ध्यै या दीक्षा साक्षान्न मोचनी ।
अनुसंधिवशाद्या च साक्षान्मोक्त्री सबीजिका ॥ 3
26.m:
Among them, the initiation which is for the achievement of consecration does not directly liberate,
while that which, by virtue of inner intention, directly liberates, is endowed with seed.

26.s:
tayobhayyā dīkṣitā ye teṣāmājīvavartanam /
vaktavyaṃ putrakādīnāṃ tanmayatvaprasiddhaye // 4
26.d:
तयोभय्या दीक्षिता ये तेषामाजीववर्तनम् ।
वक्तव्यं पुत्रकादीनां तन्मयत्वप्रसिद्धये ॥ 4
26.m:
For those who have been initiated by both kinds, the lifelong conduct
of the spiritual son and others must be stated for the accomplishment of identity with That.

26.s:
bubhukṣorvā mumukṣorvā svasaṃvidguruśāstrataḥ /
pramāṇādyā saṃskriyāyai dīkṣā hi guruṇā kṛtā // 5
26.d:
बुभुक्षोर्वा मुमुक्षोर्वा स्वसंविद्गुरुशास्त्रतः ।
प्रमाणाद्या संस्क्रियायै दीक्षा हि गुरुणा कृता ॥ 5
26.m:
Whether for one who desires enjoyment or one who desires liberation, the initiation for consecration
performed by the guru through the authority of his own consciousness, the guru, and the scriptures,

26.s:
tataḥ sa saṃskṛtaṃ yogyaṃ jñātvātmānaṃ svaśāsane /
taduktavastvanuṣṭhānaṃ bhuktyai muktyai ca sevate // 6
26.d:
ततः स संस्कृतं योग्यं ज्ञात्वात्मानं स्वशासने ।
तदुक्तवस्त्वनुष्ठानं भुक्त्यै मुक्त्यै च सेवते ॥ 6
26.m:
thereupon, knowing himself to be consecrated and qualified within his own tradition,
he practices the observance of the things taught therein for enjoyment and for liberation.

26.s:
ācāryapratyayādeva yo'pi syādbhuktimuktibhāk /
tatpratyūhodayadhvastyai brūyāttasyāpi vartanam // 7
26.d:
आचार्यप्रत्ययादेव योऽपि स्याद्भुक्तिमुक्तिभाक् ।
तत्प्रत्यूहोदयध्वस्त्यै ब्रूयात्तस्यापि वर्तनम् ॥ 7
26.m:
Even for one who partakes of enjoyment and liberation merely through conviction in the master,
one should explain the course of conduct for him too, in order to destroy the arising of obstacles to it.

26.s:
svasaṃvidgurusaṃvittyostulyapratyayabhāgapi /
śeṣavṛttyā samādeśyastadvighnādipraśāntaye // 8
26.d:
स्वसंविद्गुरुसंवित्त्योस्तुल्यप्रत्ययभागपि ।
शेषवृत्त्या समादेश्यस्तद्विघ्नादिप्रशान्तये ॥ 8
26.m: Even one who shares equal conviction in his own consciousness and the guru's consciousness / should be instructed through supplementary practice in order to pacify obstacles and the like. // 8

26.s:
yaḥ sarvathā parāpekṣāmujjhitvā tu sthito nijāt /
pratyayādyo'pi cācāryapratyayādeva kevalāt // 9
26.d:
यः सर्वथा परापेक्षामुज्झित्वा तु स्थितो निजात् ।
प्रत्ययाद्योऽपि चाचार्यप्रत्ययादेव केवलात् ॥ 9
26.m: He who remains completely abandoning dependence on another through his own / conviction, and he who does so solely through the master's conviction— // 9

26.s:
tau sāṃsiddhikanirbījau ko vadeccheṣavṛttaye /
kramāttanmayatopāyagurvarcanaratau tu tau // 10
26.d:
तौ सांसिद्धिकनिर्बीजौ को वदेच्छेषवृत्तये ।
क्रमात्तन्मयतोपायगुर्वर्चनरतौ तु तौ ॥ 10
26.m: Who would tell those two—the spontaneous and the seedless—to adopt remaining practices? / But they, in succession, are devoted to the means of identifying with That and worshipping the guru. // 10

26.s:
tatraiṣāṃ śeṣavṛttyarthaṃ nityanaimittike dhruve /
kāmyavarjaṃ yataḥ kāmāścitrāścitrābhyupāyakāḥ // 11
26.d:
तत्रैषां शेषवृत्त्यर्थं नित्यनैमित्तिके ध्रुवे ।
काम्यवर्जं यतः कामाश्चित्राश्चित्राभ्युपायकाः ॥ 11
26.m: For them, for the sake of remaining practices, the regular and occasional [rites] are constant, / excluding the optional ones, since desires are varied and have varied means. // 11

26.s:
tatra nityo vidhiḥ sandhyānuṣṭhānaṃ devatāvraje /
gurvagniśāstrasahite pūjā bhūtadayetyayam // 12
26.d:
तत्र नित्यो विधिः सन्ध्यानुष्ठानं देवताव्रजे ।
गुर्वग्निशास्त्रसहिते पूजा भूतदयेत्ययम् ॥ 12
26.m: In that regard, the regular rite is this: performance of twilight devotions, worship of the multitude of deities / together with the guru, the sacred fire, and scripture, and compassion for living beings. // 12

26.s:
naimittikastu sarveṣāṃ parvaṇāṃ pūjanaṃ japaḥ /
viśeṣavaśataḥ kiṃca pavitrakavidhikramaḥ // 13
26.d:
नैमित्तिकस्तु सर्वेषां पर्वणां पूजनं जपः ।
विशेषवशतः किंच पवित्रकविधिक्रमः ॥ 13
26.m: The occasional [rite], however, is worship and recitation on all sacred transition days, / and furthermore, according to special occasions, the sequence of the rite of the sacred thread. // 13

26.s:
ācāryasya ca dīkṣeyaṃ bahubhedā vivecitā /
vyākhyādikaṃ ca tattasyādhikaṃ naimittikaṃ dhruvam // 14
26.d:
आचार्यस्य च दीक्षेयं बहुभेदा विवेचिता ।
व्याख्यादिकं च तत्तस्याधिकं नैमित्तिकं ध्रुवम् ॥ 14
26.m: And for the master, this initiation of manifold varieties has been analyzed, / as well as exposition and the like; that is definitely his additional occasional duty. // 14

26.s:
tatrādau śiśave vrūyādgururnityavidhiṃ sphuṭam /
tadyogyatāṃ samālokya vitatāvitatātmanām // 15
26.d:
तत्रादौ शिशवे व्रूयाद्गुरुर्नित्यविधिं स्फुटम् ।
तद्योग्यतां समालोक्य वितताविततात्मनाम् ॥ 15
26.m: There, the guru should first clearly declare the regular rite to the novice, / observing his fitness, among those of extensive or non-extensive capacity. // 15

26.s:
mukhyetarādimantrāṇāṃ vīryavyāptyādiyogyatām /
dṛṣṭvā śiṣye tamevāsmai mūlamantraṃ samarpayet // 16
26.d:
मुख्येतरादिमन्त्राणां वीर्यव्याप्त्यादियोग्यताम् ।
दृष्ट्वा शिष्ये तमेवास्मै मूलमन्त्रं समर्पयेत् ॥ 16
26.m: Having observed in the disciple his capacity for the power, pervasion, and so forth / of the principal and secondary mantras, he should bestow upon him that very root mantra. // 16

26.s:
tacchāstradīkṣito hyeṣa niryantrācāraśaṅkitaḥ /
na mukhye yogya ityanyasevātaḥ syāttu yogyatā // 17
26.d:
तच्छास्त्रदीक्षितो ह्येष निर्यन्त्राचारशङ्कितः ।
न मुख्ये योग्य इत्यन्यसेवातः स्यात्तु योग्यता ॥ 17
26.m: For one initiated into that scripture, hesitant regarding unconstrained conduct, / is not fit for the principal [mantra]; but through attending upon another, fitness may arise. // 17

26.s:
sādhakasya bubhukṣostu sādhakībhāvino'pivā /
puṣpapātavaśātsiddho mantro'rpyaḥ sādhyasiddhaye // 18
26.d:
साधकस्य बुभुक्षोस्तु साधकीभाविनोऽपिवा ।
पुष्पपातवशात्सिद्धो मन्त्रोऽर्प्यः साध्यसिद्धये ॥ 18
26.m: For an adept who desires enjoyment, or one destined to become an adept, / the mantra achieved by the casting of a flower should be imparted for the attainment of the intended goal. // 18

26.s:
vitate guṇabhūte vā vidhau diṣṭe punarguruḥ /
jñātvāsmai yogyatāṃ sāraṃ saṃkṣiptaṃ vidhimācaret // 19
26.d:
वितते गुणभूते वा विधौ दिष्टे पुनर्गुरुः ।
ज्ञात्वास्मै योग्यतां सारं संक्षिप्तं विधिमाचरेत् ॥ 19
26.m: When an extensive or subsidiary rite has been designated, again the guru, / knowing his fitness, should perform the concise essence of the rite for him. // 19

26.s:
tatraiṣa niyamo yadyanmāntraṃ rūpaṃ na tadguruḥ /
likhitvā prathayecchiṣye viśeṣādūrdhvaśāsane // 20
26.d:
तत्रैष नियमो यद्यन्मान्त्रं रूपं न तद्गुरुः ।
लिखित्वा प्रथयेच्छिष्ये विशेषादूर्ध्वशासने ॥ 20
26.m: In this matter, this is the rule: whatever has the form of a mantra, the guru must not / write it down and impart it to the disciple, especially in the Northern transmission. // 20

26.s:
mantrā varṇātmakāste ca parāmarśātmakāḥ saca /
gurusaṃvidabhinnaśvetsaṃkrāmetsā tataḥ śiśau // 21
26.d:
मन्त्रा वर्णात्मकास्ते च परामर्शात्मकाः सच ।
गुरुसंविदभिन्नश्वेत्संक्रामेत्सा ततः शिशौ ॥ 21
26.m: Mantras consist of phonemes, and these consist of conscious reflection, and this / is non-different from the consciousness of the guru; then it can be transferred to the novice. // 21

26.s:
lipisthitastu yo mantro nirvīryaḥ so'tra kalpitaḥ /
saṃketabalato nāsya pustakātprathate mahaḥ // 22
26.d:
लिपिस्थितस्तु यो मन्त्रो निर्वीर्यः सोऽत्र कल्पितः ।
संकेतबलतो नास्य पुस्तकात्प्रथते महः ॥ 22
26.m: A mantra that is fixed in written letters is regarded here as powerless; / on account of convention, its glory does not emanate from a manuscript. // 22

26.s:
pustakādhītavidyāścetyuktaṃ siddhāmate tataḥ /
ye tu pustakalabdhe'pi mantre vīryaṃ prajānate // 23
26.d:
पुस्तकाधीतविद्याश्चेत्युक्तं सिद्धामते ततः ।
ये तु पुस्तकलब्धेऽपि मन्त्रे वीर्यं प्रजानते ॥ 23
26.m: Hence, it is said in the Siddhāmata: 'And the knowledges learned from books…' / But those who recognize the potency even in a mantra acquired from a book, // 23

26.s:
te bhairavīyasaṃskārāḥ proktāḥ sāṃsiddhikā iti /
iti jñātvā guruḥ samyak paramānandaghūrṇitaḥ // 24
26.d:
ते भैरवीयसंस्काराः प्रोक्ताः सांसिद्धिका इति ।
इति ज्ञात्वा गुरुः सम्यक् परमानन्दघूर्णितः ॥ 24
26.m: they, bearing the imprint of Bhairava, are proclaimed to be 'spontaneous.' / Knowing this well, the guru, reeling with supreme bliss, // 24

26.s:
tādṛśe tādṛśe dhāmni pūjayitvā vidhiṃ caret /
yathānyaśiṣyānuṣṭhānaṃ nānyaśiṣyeṇa budhyate // 25
26.d:
तादृशे तादृशे धाम्नि पूजयित्वा विधिं चरेत् ।
यथान्यशिष्यानुष्ठानं नान्यशिष्येण बुध्यते ॥ 25
26.m: having worshipped in such and such an abode, should carry out the ritual, / in such a way that the practice of one disciple is not known by another disciple. // 25

26.s:
tathā kuryādgururguptihānirdoṣavatī yataḥ /
devīnāṃ tritayaṃ śuddhaṃ yadvā yāmalayogataḥ // 26
26.d:
तथा कुर्याद्गुरुर्गुप्तिहानिर्दोषवती यतः ।
देवीनां त्रितयं शुद्धं यद्वा यामलयोगतः ॥ 26
26.m: The guru should do this, since the loss of secrecy is faulty. / [He teaches] the triad of pure goddesses, or through the union of the dyad, // 26

26.s:
devīmekāmatho śuddhāṃ vadedvā yāmalātmikām /
tatra mantraṃ sphuṭaṃ vaktrādguruṇopāṃśu coditam // 27
26.d:
देवीमेकामथो शुद्धां वदेद्वा यामलात्मिकाम् ।
तत्र मन्त्रं स्फुटं वक्त्राद्गुरुणोपांशु चोदितम् ॥ 27
26.m: or he should teach a single pure goddess, or one whose nature is the dyad. / There, having ascertained the clear mantra uttered softly from the mouth of the guru, // 27

26.s:
avadhāryā pravṛttestamabhyasyenmanasā svayam /
tataḥ suśikṣitāṃ sthānadehāntaḥśodhanatrayīm // 28
26.d:
अवधार्या प्रवृत्तेस्तमभ्यस्येन्मनसा स्वयम् ।
ततः सुशिक्षितां स्थानदेहान्तःशोधनत्रयीम् ॥ 28
26.m: the disciple himself should mentally practice it until spontaneous activation occurs. / Then, well instructed, he should diligently perform the triad of purifications—of place, body, and interior— // 28

26.s:
nyāsaṃ dhyānaṃ japaṃ mudrāṃ pūjāṃ kuryātprayatnataḥ /
tatra prabhāte saṃbudhya sveṣṭāṃ prāgdevatāṃ smaret // 29
26.d:
न्यासं ध्यानं जपं मुद्रां पूजां कुर्यात्प्रयत्नतः ।
तत्र प्रभाते संबुध्य स्वेष्टां प्राग्देवतां स्मरेत् ॥ 29
26.m: as well as installation, visualization, recitation, seal, and worship. / Waking there at dawn, he should first remember his chosen deity. // 29

26.s:
kṛtāvaśyakakartavyaḥ śuddho bhūtvā tato gṛham /
āśrityottaradigvaktraḥ sthānadehāntaratraye // 30
26.d:
कृतावश्यककर्तव्यः शुद्धो भूत्वा ततो गृहम् ।
आश्रित्योत्तरदिग्वक्त्रः स्थानदेहान्तरत्रये ॥ 30
26.m: Having performed the obligatory duties and become pure, he then enters the room, / faces the northern direction, and having performed purification in the triad of place, body, and interior, // 30

26.s:
śuddhiṃ vidhāya mantrāṇāṃ yathāsthānaṃ niveśanam /
mudrāpradarśanaṃ dhyānaṃ bhedābhedasvarūpataḥ // 31
26.d:
शुद्धिं विधाय मन्त्राणां यथास्थानं निवेशनम् ।
मुद्राप्रदर्शनं ध्यानं भेदाभेदस्वरूपतः ॥ 31
26.m: he carries out the proper placement of mantras according to location, / the exhibition of seals, and visualization according to the nature of difference and non-difference. // 31

26.s:
dehāsudhīvyomabhūṣu manasā tatra cārcanam /
japaṃ cātra yathāśakti devāyaitannivedanam // 32
26.d:
देहासुधीव्योमभूषु मनसा तत्र चार्चनम् ।
जपं चात्र यथाशक्ति देवायैतन्निवेदनम् ॥ 32
26.m: There he mentally performs worship upon the body, breath, intellect, and internal space, / and recitation here according to capacity, offering this to the deity. // 32

26.s:
tanmayībhāvasiddhyarthaṃ pratisandhyaṃ samācaret /
anye tu prāgudakpaścāddaśadikṣu catuṣṭayīm // 33
26.d:
तन्मयीभावसिद्ध्यर्थं प्रतिसन्ध्यं समाचरेत् ।
अन्ये तु प्रागुदक्पश्चाद्दशदिक्षु चतुष्टयीम् ॥ 33
26.m: He should perform this at every twilight for the sake of attaining identification with That. / Others, however, speak of a group of four twilights in the east, north, west, and south, // 33

26.s:
sandhyānāmāhuretacca tāntrikīyaṃ na no matam /
yāsau kālādhikāre prāk sandhyā proktā catuṣṭayī // 34
26.d:
सन्ध्यानामाहुरेतच्च तान्त्रिकीयं न नो मतम् ।
यासौ कालाधिकारे प्राक् सन्ध्या प्रोक्ता चतुष्टयी ॥ 34
26.m: and this belongs to the Tantric system, not our doctrine. / Composing internally only that fourfold twilight which was explained earlier in the section on Time, // 34

26.s:
tāmevāntaḥ samādhāya sāndhyaṃ vidhimupācaret /
sandhyācatuṣṭayīkṛtyamekasyāmathavā śiśuḥ // 35
26.d:
तामेवान्तः समाधाय सान्ध्यं विधिमुपाचरेत् ।
सन्ध्याचतुष्टयीकृत्यमेकस्यामथवा शिशुः ॥ 35
26.m: he should perform the twilight rite; or the novice may perform the duty of the fourfold twilight / in a single one, devoted to sacred recitation, experiential knowledge, the guru's service, and the like. // 35

26.s:
kuryātsvādhyāyavijñānagurukṛtyāditatparaḥ /
sandhyādhyānoditānantatanmayībhāvayuktitaḥ // 36
26.d:
कुर्यात्स्वाध्यायविज्ञानगुरुकृत्यादितत्परः ।
सन्ध्याध्यानोदितानन्ततन्मयीभावयुक्तितः ॥ 36
26.m: Through application of the endless identification with That arising from the twilight visualization, / he remains indeed identified with That at all times by virtue of its imprint. // 36

26.s:
tatsaṃskāravaśātsarvaṃ kālaṃ syāttanmayo hyasau /
tato yatheṣṭakāle'sau pūjāṃ puṣpāsavādibhiḥ // 37
26.d:
तत्संस्कारवशात्सर्वं कालं स्यात्तन्मयो ह्यसौ ।
ततो यथेष्टकालेऽसौ पूजां पुष्पासवादिभिः ॥ 37
26.m: Then, at any desired time, the novice should perform worship with flowers, liquors, and the like / upon a prepared ground and so forth according to his wealth and capacity, // 37

26.s:
sthaṇḍilādau śiśuḥ kuryādvibhavādyanurūpataḥ /
suśuddhaḥ sanvidhiṃ sarvaṃ kṛtvāntarajapāntakam // 38
26.d:
स्थण्डिलादौ शिशुः कुर्याद्विभवाद्यनुरूपतः ।
सुशुद्धः सन्विधिं सर्वं कृत्वान्तरजपान्तकम् ॥ 38
26.m: being well purified, having performed the entire ritual up to the conclusion of the internal recitation. / The wise one, having prepared the vessel of oblations with his chosen mantra as before, // 38

26.s:
arghapātraṃ purā yadvadvidhāya sveṣṭamantrataḥ /
tena sthaṇḍilapuṣpādi sarvaṃ saṃprokṣayedbudhaḥ // 39
26.d:
अर्घपात्रं पुरा यद्वद्विधाय स्वेष्टमन्त्रतः ।
तेन स्थण्डिलपुष्पादि सर्वं संप्रोक्षयेद्बुधः ॥ 39
26.m: should sprinkle everything with it—the ground, flowers, and the rest. / Then, envisioning right there the sequence of doors, seat, and gurus, // 39

26.s:
tatastatraiva saṃkalpya dvārāsanagurukramam /
pūjayecchivatāviṣṭaḥ svadehārcāpuraḥsaram // 40
26.d:
ततस्तत्रैव संकल्प्य द्वारासनगुरुक्रमम् ।
पूजयेच्छिवताविष्टः स्वदेहार्चापुरःसरम् ॥ 40
26.m: filled with Śivahood, he should worship, preceded by the worship of his own body. / Then, beholding that prepared ground as clear as pure sky and crystal, // 40

26.s:
tatastatsthaṇḍilaṃ vīdhravyomasphaṭikanirmalam /
bodhātmakaṃ samālokya tatra svaṃ devatāgaṇam // 41
26.d:
ततस्तत्स्थण्डिलं वीध्रव्योमस्फटिकनिर्मलम् ।
बोधात्मकं समालोक्य तत्र स्वं देवतागणम् ॥ 41
26.m: having the nature of consciousness, he should see his own group of deities there / as a reflection, and through consciousness, as the original image. // 41

26.s:
pratibimbatayā paśyedbimbatvena ca bodhataḥ /
etadāvāhanaṃ mukhyaṃ vyajanānmarutāmiva // 42
26.d:
प्रतिबिम्बतया पश्येद्बिम्बत्वेन च बोधतः ।
एतदावाहनं मुख्यं व्यजनान्मरुतामिव ॥ 42
26.m: This is the principal invocation, just as of the wind by means of a fan. / Just as the wind, although omnipresent, becomes efficacious when drawn forth by a fan, // 42

26.s:
sarvago'pi marudyadvadvyajanenopajīvitaḥ /
arthakṛtsarvagaṃ mantracakraṃ rūḍhestathā bhavet // 43
26.d:
सर्वगोऽपि मरुद्यद्वद्व्यजनेनोपजीवितः ।
अर्थकृत्सर्वगं मन्त्रचक्रं रूढेस्तथा भवेत् ॥ 43
26.m: so the omnipresent wheel of mantras becomes [efficacious] through fixation. / This very reality is taught by the Catuṣkapañcāśikā, // 43

26.s:
catuṣkapañcāśikayā tadetattattvamucyate /
śrīnirmaryādaśāstre ca tadetadvibhunoditam // 44
26.d:
चतुष्कपञ्चाशिकया तदेतत्तत्त्वमुच्यते ।
श्रीनिर्मर्यादशास्त्रे च तदेतद्विभुनोदितम् ॥ 44
26.m: and in the venerable Nirmaryādaśāstra this very thing was spoken by the Lord. / When asked: 'O God, the God Śiva is omnipresent and unconstrained; how is he invoked // 44

26.s:
devaḥ sarvagato deva nirmaryādaḥ kathaṃ śivaḥ /
āvāhyate kṣamyate vetyevaṃpṛṣṭo'bravīdvibhuḥ // 45
26.d:
देवः सर्वगतो देव निर्मर्यादः कथं शिवः ।
आवाह्यते क्षम्यते वेत्येवंपृष्टोऽब्रवीद्विभुः ॥ 45
26.m: or dismissed?', the Lord said: / 'O Goddess, latent impression is invoked, and latent impression is dismissed. // 45

26.s:
vāsanāvāhyate devi vāsanā ca visṛjyate /
paramārthena devasya nāvāhanavisarjane // 46
26.d:
वासनावाह्यते देवि वासना च विसृज्यते ।
परमार्थेन देवस्य नावाहनविसर्जने ॥ 46
26.m: In absolute truth, there is neither invocation nor dismissal of the God. / "The God has been invoked by me, established upon the ground, // 46

26.s:
āvāhito mayā devaḥ sthaṇḍile ca pratiṣṭhitaḥ /
pūjitaḥ stuta ityevaṃ hṛṣṭvā devaṃ visarjayet // 47
26.d:
आवाहितो मया देवः स्थण्डिले च प्रतिष्ठितः ।
पूजितः स्तुत इत्येवं हृष्ट्वा देवं विसर्जयेत् ॥ 47
26.m: worshipped, and praised"—rejoicing thus, one should dismiss the God. / Invocation and the like are indeed for producing satisfaction in unawakened living beings; // 47

26.s:
prāṇināmaprabuddhānāṃ santoṣajananāya vai /
āvāhanādikaṃ teṣāṃ pravṛttiḥ kathamanyathā // 48
26.d:
प्राणिनामप्रबुद्धानां सन्तोषजननाय वै ।
आवाहनादिकं तेषां प्रवृत्तिः कथमन्यथा ॥ 48
26.m: how else would their engagement occur? / In time, however, those engaged in the Lord's teaching understand // 48

26.s:
kālena tu vijānanti pravṛttāḥ patiśāsane /
anukrameṇa devasya prāptiṃ bhuvanapūrvikām // 49
26.d:
कालेन तु विजानन्ति प्रवृत्ताः पतिशासने ।
अनुक्रमेण देवस्य प्राप्तिं भुवनपूर्विकाम् ॥ 49
26.m: the gradual attainment of the God, beginning with the cosmic worlds, / their entire accumulation of ignorance destroyed by the radiance of the lamp of knowledge. // 49

26.s:
jñānadīpadyutidhvastasamastājñānasañcayāḥ /
kuto vānīyate devaḥ kutra vā nīyate'pi saḥ // 50
26.d:
ज्ञानदीपद्युतिध्वस्तसमस्ताज्ञानसञ्चयाः ।
कुतो वानीयते देवः कुत्र वा नीयतेऽपि सः ॥ 50
26.m: From where would the God be brought, or to where would he be taken? / For he resides everywhere through distinctions such as gross and subtle.' // 50

26.s:
sthūlasūkṣmādibhedena sa hi sarvatra saṃsthitaḥ /
āvāhite mantragaṇe puṣpāsavanivedanaiḥ // 51
26.d:
स्थूलसूक्ष्मादिभेदेन स हि सर्वत्र संस्थितः ।
आवाहिते मन्त्रगणे पुष्पासवनिवेदनैः ॥ 51
26.m: When the assembly of mantras has been invoked, propitiation must be made with offerings of flowers and liquor, / and with incenses, suited to the strength of faith and devotion. // 51

26.s:
dhūpaiśca tarpaṇaṃ kāryaṃ śraddhābhaktibalocitaiḥ /
dīptānāṃ śaktinādādimantrāṇāmāsavaiḥ palaiḥ // 52
26.d:
धूपैश्च तर्पणं कार्यं श्रद्धाभक्तिबलोचितैः ।
दीप्तानां शक्तिनादादिमन्त्राणामासवैः पलैः ॥ 52
26.m: Propitiation of the blazing mantras of Śakti, Nāda, and the rest is performed first with liquors, flesh, / and blood, and afterwards with the elaborate offerings of flowers, incense, and the like. // 52

26.s:
raktaiḥ prāk tarpaṇa paścāt puṣpadhūpādivistaraiḥ /
āgatasya tu mantrasya na kuryāttarpaṇaṃ yadi // 53
26.d:
रक्तैः प्राक् तर्पण पश्चात् पुष्पधूपादिविस्तरैः ।
आगतस्य तु मन्त्रस्य न कुर्यात्तर्पणं यदि ॥ 53
26.m: If one does not perform the propitiation of the arrived mantra, // 53

26.s:
haratyardhaśarīraṃ sa ityuktaṃ kila śambhunā /
yadyadevāsya manasi vikāsitvaṃ prayacchati // 54
26.d:
हरत्यर्धशरीरं स इत्युक्तं किल शम्भुना ।
यद्यदेवास्य मनसि विकासित्वं प्रयच्छति ॥ 54
26.m: ‘He takes away half of [that person's] body’—so it is said by Śambhu. / Whatever brings about expansion in his mind, // 54

26.s:
tenaiva kuryātpūjāṃ sa iti śambhorviniścayaḥ /
sādhakānāṃ bubhukṣūṇāṃ vidhirniyatiyantritaḥ // 55
26.d:
तेनैव कुर्यात्पूजां स इति शम्भोर्विनिश्चयः ।
साधकानां बुभुक्षूणां विधिर्नियतियन्त्रितः ॥ 55
26.m: with that very thing he should perform the worship: such is the determination of Śambhu. / For adepts desirous of enjoyment, the rule is bound by cosmic order (niyati); // 55

26.s:
mumukṣūṇāṃ tattvavidāṃ sa eva tu nirargalaḥ /
kārye viśeṣamādhitsurviśiṣṭaṃ kāraṇaṃ spṛśet // 56
26.d:
मुमुक्षूणां तत्त्वविदां स एव तु निरर्गलः ।
कार्ये विशेषमाधित्सुर्विशिष्टं कारणं स्पृशेत् ॥ 56
26.m: but for those desirous of liberation who know reality, that very rule is unhindered. / One who wishes to produce a particular effect should make use of a specific cause, // 56

26.s:
raktakarpāsatūlecchustulyatadbījapuñjavat /
santi bhoge viśeṣāśca vicitrāḥ kāraṇeritāḥ // 57
26.d:
रक्तकर्पासतूलेच्छुस्तुल्यतद्बीजपुञ्जवत् ।
सन्ति भोगे विशेषाश्च विचित्राः कारणेरिताः ॥ 57
26.m: just as one who desires red cotton wool [uses] a corresponding heap of its seeds. / In enjoyment there are indeed various distinctions prompted by causes, // 57

26.s:
deśakālānusandhānaguṇadravyakriyādibhiḥ /
svalpā kriyā bhūyasī vā hṛdayāhlādadāyibhiḥ // 58
26.d:
देशकालानुसन्धानगुणद्रव्यक्रियादिभिः ।
स्वल्पा क्रिया भूयसी वा हृदयाह्लाददायिभिः ॥ 58
26.m: through the integration of place and time, quality, substance, action, and the like. / An action, whether small or great, arranged by factors of action that give delight to the heart— // 58

26.s:
bāhyaiḥ saṃkalpajairvāpi kārakaiḥ parikalpitā /
mumukṣorna viśeṣāya naiḥśreyasavidhiṃ prati // 59
26.d:
बाह्यैः संकल्पजैर्वापि कारकैः परिकल्पिता ।
मुमुक्षोर्न विशेषाय नैःश्रेयसविधिं प्रति ॥ 59
26.m: whether external or born of mental intention— / makes no difference for the seeker of liberation with regard to the path to the highest good. // 59

26.s:
nahi brahmaṇi śaṃsanti bāhulyālpatvadurdaśāḥ /
