citaḥ svātantryasāratvāt tasyānandaghanatvataḥ // 60
26.d:
नहि ब्रह्मणि शंसन्ति बाहुल्याल्पत्वदुर्दशाः ।
चितः स्वातन्त्र्यसारत्वात् तस्यानन्दघनत्वतः ॥ 60
26.m: For the defective conditions of abundance and deficiency are not praised in Brahman, / because consciousness has absolute autonomy as its essence, and because it is a mass of bliss. // 60

26.s:
kriyā syāttanmayībhūtyai hṛdayāhlādadāyibhiḥ /
śivābhedabharādbhāvavargaḥ ścyotati yaṃ rasam // 61
26.d:
क्रिया स्यात्तन्मयीभूत्यै हृदयाह्लाददायिभिः ।
शिवाभेदभराद्भाववर्गः श्च्योतति यं रसम् ॥ 61
26.m: Action should lead to identification with that, through things that give delight to the heart. / The nectar that the multitude of existent things exudes due to the weight of non-duality with Śiva, // 61

26.s:
tameva parame dhāmni pūjanāyārpayedbudhaḥ /
stotreṣu bahudhā caitanmayā proktaṃ nijāhnike // 62
26.d:
तमेव परमे धाम्नि पूजनायार्पयेद्बुधः ।
स्तोत्रेषु बहुधा चैतन्मया प्रोक्तं निजाह्निके ॥ 62
26.m: that very [nectar] the wise person should offer for worship in the supreme abode. / And this has been stated by me in many ways in the hymns in my own daily lesson: // 62

26.s:
adhiśayya pāramārthikabhāvaprasaraprakāśamullasati /
yā paramāmṛtadṛk tvāṃ tayārcayante rahasyavidaḥ // 63
26.d:
अधिशय्य पारमार्थिकभावप्रसरप्रकाशमुल्लसति ।
या परमामृतदृक् त्वां तयार्चयन्ते रहस्यविदः ॥ 63
26.m: ‘Resting upon the radiance of the expansion of ultimate reality, there flashes forth / that vision of supreme nectar, with which the knowers of the secret worship you.’ // 63

26.s:
kṛtvādhāradharāṃ camatkṛtirasaprokṣākṣaṇakṣālitāmāttairmānasataḥ svabhāvakusumaiḥ svāmodasandohibhiḥ /
ānandāmṛtanirbharasvahṛdayānarghārghapātrakramāt tvāṃ devyā saha dehadevasadane devārcaye'harniśam // 64
26.d:
कृत्वाधारधरां चमत्कृतिरसप्रोक्षाक्षणक्षालितामात्तैर्मानसतः स्वभावकुसुमैः स्वामोदसन्दोहिभिः ।
आनन्दामृतनिर्भरस्वहृदयानर्घार्घपात्रक्रमात् त्वां देव्या सह देहदेवसदने देवार्चयेऽहर्निशम् ॥ 64
26.m: ‘Having made the ground of the support washed in an instant by the sprinkling of the juice of wonder, with flowers of one's own nature gathered from the mind and abounding in their own fragrance, / by means of an unpriced vessel of oblations that is one's own heart filled with the nectar of bliss, O God, along with the Goddess, I worship you day and night in the temple of the body.’ // 64

26.s:
nānāsvādarasāmimāṃ trijagatīṃ hṛccakrayantrārpitāmūrdhvādhyastavivekagauravabharānniṣpīḍya niḥṣyanditam /
yatsaṃvitparamāmṛtaṃ mṛtijarājanmāpahaṃ jṛmbhate tena tvāṃ haviṣā pareṇa parame saṃtarpaye'harniśam // 65
26.d:
नानास्वादरसामिमां त्रिजगतीं हृच्चक्रयन्त्रार्पितामूर्ध्वाध्यस्तविवेकगौरवभरान्निष्पीड्य निःष्यन्दितम् ।
यत्संवित्परमामृतं मृतिजराजन्मापहं जृम्भते तेन त्वां हविषा परेण परमे संतर्पयेऽहर्निशम् ॥ 65
26.m: ‘Having placed this threefold world, rich in flavors of diverse tastes, into the press of the heart-wheel, and having squeezed it out under the crushing weight of discernment placed above it, / whatever supreme nectar of consciousness unfolds, dispelling death, old age, and birth, with that supreme offering I satiate you day and night in the Supreme, [O Lord]!’ // 65

26.s:
iti ślokatrayopāttamarthamantarvibhāvayan /
yena kenāpi bhāvena tarpayeddevatāgaṇam // 66
26.d:
इति श्लोकत्रयोपात्तमर्थमन्तर्विभावयन् ।
येन केनापि भावेन तर्पयेद्देवतागणम् ॥ 66
26.m: Contemplating internally the meaning conveyed by these three verses, / one should satisfy the host of deities through any state whatsoever. // 66

26.s:
mudrāṃ pradarśayetpaścānmanasā vāpi yogataḥ /
vacasā mantrayogena vapuṣā saṃniveśataḥ // 67
26.d:
मुद्रां प्रदर्शयेत्पश्चान्मनसा वापि योगतः ।
वचसा मन्त्रयोगेन वपुषा संनिवेशतः ॥ 67
26.m: Afterwards he should show the mudrā, either with the mind through yogic union, / or with speech through the union of mantra, or with the body through posture. // 67

26.s:
kṛtvā japaṃ tataḥ sarvaṃ devatāyai samarpayet /
taccoktaṃ kartṛtātattvanirūpaṇavidhau purā // 68
26.d:
कृत्वा जपं ततः सर्वं देवतायै समर्पयेत् ।
तच्चोक्तं कर्तृतातत्त्वनिरूपणविधौ पुरा ॥ 68
26.m: Having performed recitation, he should then surrender everything to the deity. / And that was spoken of previously in the chapter setting forth the reality of agency. // 68

26.s:
tato visarjanaṃ kāryaṃ bodhaikātmyaprayogataḥ /
kṛtvā vā vahnigāṃ mantratṛptiṃ proktavidhānataḥ // 69
26.d:
ततो विसर्जनं कार्यं बोधैकात्म्यप्रयोगतः ।
कृत्वा वा वह्निगां मन्त्रतृप्तिं प्रोक्तविधानतः ॥ 69
26.m: Then the dismissal must be performed through the application of unity with awareness, / or having performed the satisfaction of mantras entering the fire according to the prescribed rule. // 69

26.s:
dvārapīṭhaguruvrātasamarpitanivedanāt /
ṛte'nyatsvayamaśnīyādagādhe'mbhasyatha kṣipet // 70
26.d:
द्वारपीठगुरुव्रातसमर्पितनिवेदनात् ।
ऋतेऽन्यत्स्वयमश्नीयादगाधेऽम्भस्यथ क्षिपेत् ॥ 70
26.m: Except for the offering made to the doorway, the seat, and the assembly of gurus, / he should eat the rest himself, or cast it into deep water. // 70

26.s:
prāṇino jalajāḥ pūrvadīkṣitāḥ śambhunā svayam /
vidhinā bhāvinā śrīmanmīnanāthāvatāriṇā // 71
26.d:
प्राणिनो जलजाः पूर्वदीक्षिताः शम्भुना स्वयम् ।
विधिना भाविना श्रीमन्मीननाथावतारिणा ॥ 71
26.m: Living beings born in water were previously initiated by Śambhu himself / through the prospective rite when he descended as the illustrious Mīnanātha. // 71

26.s:
mārjāramūṣikādyairyadadīkṣaiścāpi bhakṣitam /
tacchaṅkātaṅkadānena vyādhaye narakāya ca // 72
26.d:
मार्जारमूषिकाद्यैर्यददीक्षैश्चापि भक्षितम् ।
तच्छङ्कातङ्कदानेन व्याधये नरकाय च ॥ 72
26.m: Whatever is eaten by uninitiated creatures such as cats and mice, / that, by producing the anguish of doubt, leads to disease and hell. // 72

26.s:
atastattvavidā dhvastaśaṅkātaṅko'pi paṇḍitaḥ /
prakaṭaṃ nedṛśaṃ kuryāllokānugrahavāñchayā // 73
26.d:
अतस्तत्त्वविदा ध्वस्तशङ्कातङ्कोऽपि पण्डितः ।
प्रकटं नेदृशं कुर्याल्लोकानुग्रहवाञ्छया ॥ 73
26.m: Therefore the learned person who knows reality, even though his anguish of doubt is destroyed, / should not do such a thing openly, out of a desire to show grace to the world. // 73

26.s:
śrīmanmatamahāśāstre taduktaṃ vibhunā svayam /
svayaṃ tu śaṅkāsaṅkocaniṣkāsanaparāyaṇaḥ // 74
26.d:
श्रीमन्मतमहाशास्त्रे तदुक्तं विभुना स्वयम् ।
स्वयं तु शङ्कासङ्कोचनिष्कासनपरायणः ॥ 74
26.m: In the illustrious Matamahāśāstra that has been stated by the all-pervading Lord himself. / But he himself, devoted to expelling the contraction of doubt, // 74

26.s:
bhavettathā yathānyeṣāṃ śaṅkā no manasi sphuret /
mārjayitvā tataḥ snānaṃ puṣpeṇātha prapūjayet // 75
26.d:
भवेत्तथा यथान्येषां शङ्का नो मनसि स्फुरेत् ।
मार्जयित्वा ततः स्नानं पुष्पेणाथ प्रपूजयेत् ॥ 75
26.m: should be such that doubt does not flash forth in the minds of others. / Then, having cleansed [the place], taking a bath, he should worship with a flower. // 75

26.s:
puṣpādi sarvaṃ tatsthaṃ tadagādhāmbhasi nikṣipet /
uktaḥ sthaṇḍilayāgo'yaṃ nityakarmaṇi śambhunā // 76
26.d:
पुष्पादि सर्वं तत्स्थं तदगाधाम्भसि निक्षिपेत् ।
उक्तः स्थण्डिलयागोऽयं नित्यकर्मणि शम्भुना ॥ 76
26.m: He should cast everything situated there, such as flowers, into deep water. / This ground sacrifice in the daily ritual has been taught by Śambhu. // 76

27.s: athocyate liṅgapūjā sūcitā mālinīmate // 1
27.d: अथोच्यते लिङ्गपूजा सूचिता मालिनीमते ॥ 1
27.m: Now the worship of the liṅga indicated in the Mālinī doctrine is explained. // 1b

27.s:
eteṣāmūrdhvaśāstroktamantrāṇāṃ na pratiṣṭhitam /
bahiṣkuryāttato hyete rahasyatvena siddhidāḥ // 2
27.d:
एतेषामूर्ध्वशास्त्रोक्तमन्त्राणां न प्रतिष्ठितम् ।
बहिष्कुर्यात्ततो ह्येते रहस्यत्वेन सिद्धिदाः ॥ 2
27.m: One should not externalize the consecration of these mantras spoken in the superior teachings; / for these bestow spiritual accomplishment by virtue of their secret nature. // 2

27.s:
svavīryānandamāhātmyapraveśavaśaśālinīm /
ye siddhiṃ dadate teṣāṃ bāhyatvaṃ rūpavicyutiḥ // 3
27.d:
स्ववीर्यानन्दमाहात्म्यप्रवेशवशशालिनीम् ।
ये सिद्धिं ददते तेषां बाह्यत्वं रूपविच्युतिः ॥ 3
27.m: For those [mantras] which grant spiritual accomplishment possessed of the mastery that enters the greatness of their own potency's bliss, / externalization is a loss of their true form. // 3

27.s:
kiṃca coktaṃ samāveśapūrṇo bhoktrātmakaḥ śivaḥ /
bhogalāmpaṭyabhāgbhogavicchede nigrahātmakaḥ // 4
27.d:
किंच चोक्तं समावेशपूर्णो भोक्त्रात्मकः शिवः ।
भोगलाम्पट्यभाग्भोगविच्छेदे निग्रहात्मकः ॥ 4
27.m: Moreover, it is said: Śiva is filled with immersion, having the nature of the enjoyer; / he partakes of attachment to enjoyment, and in the cessation of enjoyment he has the nature of restraint. // 4

27.s:
śāntatvanyakkriyodbhūtajighatsāvṛṃhitaṃ vapuḥ /
svayaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ yena so'syābhoge vinaśyati // 5
27.d:
शान्तत्वन्यक्क्रियोद्भूतजिघत्सावृंहितं वपुः ।
स्वयं प्रतिष्ठितं येन सोऽस्याभोगे विनश्यति ॥ 5
27.m: One who himself consecrates [an external form] when his body is augmented by hunger arising from the suppression of calm state, / perishes in the absence of enjoyment of this [deity]. // 5

27.s:
uktaṃ jñānottarāyāṃ ca tadetatparameśinā /
śivo yāgapriyo yasmādviśeṣānmātṛmadhyagaḥ // 6
27.d:
उक्तं ज्ञानोत्तरायां च तदेतत्परमेशिना ।
शिवो यागप्रियो यस्माद्विशेषान्मातृमध्यगः ॥ 6
27.m: And this was spoken by the Supreme Lord in the Jñānottarā: / ‘Because Śiva is fond of sacrifice, especially when situated in the midst of the Mothers, // 6

27.s:
tasmādrahasyaśāstreṣu ye mantrāstānbudho bahiḥ /
na pratiṣṭhāpayejjātu viśeṣādvyaktarūpiṇaḥ // 7
27.d:
तस्माद्रहस्यशास्त्रेषु ये मन्त्रास्तान्बुधो बहिः ।
न प्रतिष्ठापयेज्जातु विशेषाद्व्यक्तरूपिणः ॥ 7
27.m: therefore, the mantras that are in the secret teachings, the wise person should never / consecrate externally, especially those that have a manifest form.’ // 7

27.s:
ata eva mṛtasyārthe pratiṣṭhānyatra yoditā /
sātra śāstreṣu no kāryā kāryā sādhāraṇī punaḥ // 8
27.d:
अत एव मृतस्यार्थे प्रतिष्ठान्यत्र योदिता ।
सात्र शास्त्रेषु नो कार्या कार्या साधारणी पुनः ॥ 8
27.m: Precisely for this reason, the consecration prescribed elsewhere for the deceased / should not be performed in these scriptures; the common [consecration], however, should be performed. // 8

27.s:
ā tanmayatvasaṃsiddherā cābhīṣṭaphalodayāt /
putrakaḥ sādhako vyaktamavyaktaṃ vā samāśrayet // 9
27.d:
आ तन्मयत्वसंसिद्धेरा चाभीष्टफलोदयात् ।
पुत्रकः साधको व्यक्तमव्यक्तं वा समाश्रयेत् ॥ 9
27.m: Until the accomplishment of identification with that, and until the arising of the desired fruit, / the spiritual son and the adept may resort to a manifest or unmanifest [liṅga]. // 9

27.s:
putrakairgururabhyarthyaḥ sādhakastu svayaṃ vidan /
yadi tatsthāpayenno cettenāpyarthyo gururbhavet // 10
27.d:
पुत्रकैर्गुरुरभ्यर्थ्यः साधकस्तु स्वयं विदन् ।
यदि तत्स्थापयेन्नो चेत्तेनाप्यर्थ्यो गुरुर्भवेत् ॥ 10
27.m: The guru is to be requested by spiritual sons, but the adept, knowing it himself, / may establish it; if not, the guru should be requested by him as well. // 10

27.s:
guruścātra nirodhākhye kāla itthaṃ vibhau vadet /
jīvatyasminphalāntaṃ tvaṃ tiṣṭherjīvāvadhīti vā // 11
27.d:
गुरुश्चात्र निरोधाख्ये काल इत्थं विभौ वदेत् ।
जीवत्यस्मिन्फलान्तं त्वं तिष्ठेर्जीवावधीति वा ॥ 11
27.m: And in this [rite] called confinement, the guru should speak thus to the all-pervading Lord regarding time: / ‘While he lives, you should stay until the fruit is achieved,’ or ‘until the end of his life.’ // 11

27.s:
liṅgaṃ ca bāṇaliṅgaṃ vā ratnajaṃ vātha mauktikam /
pauṣpamānnamatho vāstraṃ gandhadravyakṛtaṃ ca vā // 12
27.d:
लिङ्गं च बाणलिङ्गं वा रत्नजं वाथ मौक्तिकम् ।
पौष्पमान्नमथो वास्त्रं गन्धद्रव्यकृतं च वा ॥ 12
27.m: And the liṅga may be a bāṇaliṅga, or made of jewel, or of pearl, / made of flowers, or of cooked food, or of cloth, or made of fragrant substances; // 12

27.s:
natu pāṣāṇajaṃ liṅgaṃ śilpyutthaṃ parikalpayet /
dhātūtthaṃ ca suvarṇotthavarjamanyadvivarjayet // 13
27.d:
नतु पाषाणजं लिङ्गं शिल्प्युत्थं परिकल्पयेत् ।
धातूत्थं च सुवर्णोत्थवर्जमन्यद्विवर्जयेत् ॥ 13
27.m: but one should not fashion a stone liṅga produced by a sculptor, / and as for that produced from metals, one should avoid all except that made of gold. // 13

27.s:
na cātra liṅgamānādi kvacidapyupayujyate /
udāravīryairmantrairyadbhāsitaṃ phaladaṃ hi tat // 14
27.d:
न चात्र लिङ्गमानादि क्वचिदप्युपयुज्यते ।
उदारवीर्यैर्मन्त्रैर्यद्भासितं फलदं हि तत् ॥ 14
27.m: Nor is the measurement or the like of the liṅga useful anywhere here; / for whatever is illumined by mantras of noble potency indeed yields fruit. // 14

27.s:
tasyāpi sthaṇḍilādyuktavidhinā śuddhimācaret /
mantrārpaṇaṃ tathaiva syānnirodhastūktayuktitaḥ // 15
27.d:
तस्यापि स्थण्डिलाद्युक्तविधिना शुद्धिमाचरेत् ।
मन्त्रार्पणं तथैव स्यान्निरोधस्तूक्तयुक्तितः ॥ 15
27.m: One should perform its purification as well according to the rule taught for the bare ground and the rest; / the assignment of mantras is likewise, but confinement is according to the stated method. // 15

27.s:
agnau ca tarpaṇaṃ bhūriviśeṣāddakṣiṇā guroḥ /
dīnāditṛptirvibhavādyāga ityadhiko vidhiḥ // 16
27.d:
अग्नौ च तर्पणं भूरिविशेषाद्दक्षिणा गुरोः ।
दीनादितृप्तिर्विभवाद्याग इत्यधिको विधिः ॥ 16
27.m: Abundant satisfaction in the fire, especially a sacrificial fee for the guru, / and the satisfaction of the poor and others according to wealth: this is the additional rule for the sacrifice. // 16

27.s:
sarveṣvavyaktaliṅgeṣu pradhānaṃ syādakalpitam /
tathā ca tatra tatroktaṃ lakṣaṇe pārameśvare // 17
27.d:
सर्वेष्वव्यक्तलिङ्गेषु प्रधानं स्यादकल्पितम् ।
तथा च तत्र तत्रोक्तं लक्षणे पारमेश्वरे ॥ 17
27.m: Among all unmanifest liṅgas, the unconstructed is principal. / And so it is declared in various places in the characteristics of the Supreme Lord: // 17

27.s:
sūtre pātre dhvaje vastre svayambhūbāṇapūjite /
nadīprasravaṇotthe ca nāhvānaṃ nāpi kalpanā // 18
27.d:
सूत्रे पात्रे ध्वजे वस्त्रे स्वयम्भूबाणपूजिते ।
नदीप्रस्रवणोत्थे च नाह्वानं नापि कल्पना ॥ 18
27.m: In a thread, a vessel, a banner, a cloth, in that which is self-manifest and worshipped as a bāṇa, / and in that arising from a river or a mountain torrent, there is neither invocation nor fashioning, // 18

27.s:
pīṭhaprasādamantrāṃśavelādiniyamo naca /
vyaktaṃ vā citrapustādau devadārusuvarṇajam // 19
27.d:
पीठप्रसादमन्त्रांशवेलादिनियमो नच ।
व्यक्तं वा चित्रपुस्तादौ देवदारुसुवर्णजम् ॥ 19
27.m: nor is there any rule regarding the seat, the sanctum, parts of mantras, time, and so forth. / Or [it may be] a manifest [image] in a painting, a manuscript, and the like, or made of deodar wood or gold. // 19

27.s:
atha dīkṣitasacchilpikṛtaṃ sthāpayate guruḥ /
athavā lakṣaṇopetamūrdhatatkarparāśritam // 20
27.d:
अथ दीक्षितसच्छिल्पिकृतं स्थापयते गुरुः ।
अथवा लक्षणोपेतमूर्धतत्कर्पराश्रितम् ॥ 20
27.m: Now, the guru establishes [an image] made by an initiated, good sculptor; / or, endowed with the characteristics, placed upon an upper skull, // 20

27.s:
paṅkticakrakaśūlābjavidhinā tūramāśrayet /
tallakṣaṇaṃ bruve śrīmatpicuśāstre nirūpitam // 21
27.d:
पङ्क्तिचक्रकशूलाब्जविधिना तूरमाश्रयेत् ।
तल्लक्षणं ब्रुवे श्रीमत्पिचुशास्त्रे निरूपितम् ॥ 21
27.m: he should resort to the tūra according to the rule of the series, cakra, trident, and lotus. / I shall explain its characteristics as set forth in the venerable Picu scripture. // 21

27.s:
tūre yogaḥ sadā śastaḥ siddhido doṣavarjite /
jālakairjarjarai randhrairdantairūnādhikai rujā // 22
27.d:
तूरे योगः सदा शस्तः सिद्धिदो दोषवर्जिते ।
जालकैर्जर्जरै रन्ध्रैर्दन्तैरूनाधिकै रुजा ॥ 22
27.m: the use of a skull-cup is always praised when free of defects, granting accomplishment; / but if the skull-cup is accompanied by webs of cracks, holes, deficient or excess teeth, or disease, // 22

27.s:
yukte ca tūre hāniḥ syāt taddhīne yāga uttamaḥ /
kāmya eva bhavettūramiti kecitprapedire // 23
27.d:
युक्ते च तूरे हानिः स्यात् तद्धीने याग उत्तमः ।
काम्य एव भवेत्तूरमिति केचित्प्रपेदिरे ॥ 23
27.m: there would be harm; without those, the sacrifice is highest. / Some have maintained that the skull-cup is used only for optional rites. // 23

27.s:
guravastu vidhau kāmye yatnāddoṣāṃstyajediti /
vyācakṣate picuproktaṃ na nitye karmaṇītyadaḥ // 24
27.d:
गुरवस्तु विधौ काम्ये यत्नाद्दोषांस्त्यजेदिति ।
व्याचक्षते पिचुप्रोक्तं न नित्ये कर्मणीत्यदः ॥ 24
27.m: The gurus, however, explain that the instruction taught in the Picu— / that one should diligently avoid flaws in desire-driven rites—does not apply to obligatory rites.

27.s:
śrīsiddhātantra uktaṃ ca tūralakṣaṇamuttamam /
ekādikacatuṣkhaṇḍe gomukhe pūrṇacandrake // 25
27.d:
श्रीसिद्धातन्त्र उक्तं च तूरलक्षणमुत्तमम् ।
एकादिकचतुष्खण्डे गोमुखे पूर्णचन्द्रके ॥ 25
27.m: And in the venerable Siddhātantra the excellent characteristics of the trumpet-shell are taught: / having one to four segments, shaped like a cow's mouth, like the full moon,

27.s:
padmagorocanāmuktānīrasphaṭikasaṃnibhe /
ekādipañcasadrandhravidyārekhānvite śubhe // 26
27.d:
पद्मगोरोचनामुक्तानीरस्फटिकसंनिभे ।
एकादिपञ्चसद्रन्ध्रविद्यारेखान्विते शुभे ॥ 26
27.m: resembling a lotus, bile-pigment, pearl, water, or crystal, / endowed with auspicious विद्या-lines having one to five good perforations,

27.s:
na rūkṣavakraśakaladīrghanimnasabinduke /
ślakṣṇayā vajrasūcyātra sphuṭaṃ devīgaṇānvitam // 27
27.d:
न रूक्षवक्रशकलदीर्घनिम्नसबिन्दुके ।
श्लक्ष्णया वज्रसूच्यात्र स्फुटं देवीगणान्वितम् ॥ 27
27.m: free from roughness, crookedness, chipped pieces, excessive length, hollows, or dark spots. / With a smooth diamond needle one should clearly inscribe here, along with the retinue of goddesses,

27.s:
sarvaṃ samālikhetpūjyaṃ sarvāvayavasundaram /
etadevānusartavyamarghapātre'pi lakṣaṇam // 28
27.d:
सर्वं समालिखेत्पूज्यं सर्वावयवसुन्दरम् ।
एतदेवानुसर्तव्यमर्घपात्रेऽपि लक्षणम् ॥ 28
27.m: all that is to be worshipped, beautiful in every limb. / This very same characteristic is to be observed for the vessel of offering.

27.s:
śrībrahmayāmale'pyuktaṃ pātraṃ gomukhamuttamam /
gajakūrmatalaṃ kumbhavṛttaśaktikajākṛti // 29
27.d:
श्रीब्रह्मयामलेऽप्युक्तं पात्रं गोमुखमुत्तमम् ।
गजकूर्मतलं कुम्भवृत्तशक्तिकजाकृति ॥ 29
27.m: In the venerable Brahmayāmala also the excellent vessel is stated to be shaped like a cow's mouth, / with a base like an elephant or a tortoise, and shaped like a round jar or a śaktikā-shell.

27.s:
akṣasūtramatho kuryāttatraivābhyarcayetkramam /
vīradhātujalodbhūtamuktāratnasuvarṇajam // 30
27.d:
अक्षसूत्रमथो कुर्यात्तत्रैवाभ्यर्चयेत्क्रमम् ।
वीरधातुजलोद्भूतमुक्तारत्नसुवर्णजम् ॥ 30
27.m: Next, one should make a rosary and worship the transmission on it alone: / made of [red] cinnabar, water-born pearls, jewels, or gold,

27.s:
akṣasūtraṃ kramotkṛṣṭaṃ raudrākṣaṃ vā viśeṣataḥ /
śataṃ tithyuttaraṃ yadvā sāṣṭaṃ yadvā tadardhakam // 31
27.d:
अक्षसूत्रं क्रमोत्कृष्टं रौद्राक्षं वा विशेषतः ।
शतं तिथ्युत्तरं यद्वा साष्टं यद्वा तदर्धकम् ॥ 31
27.m: the rosary is supreme in the transmission, or especially one of rudrākṣa beads: / one hundred and fifteen, or [one hundred] and eight, or half of that,

27.s:
tadardhaṃ vātha pañcāśadyuktaṃ tatparikalpayet /
vaktrāṇi pañca citspandajñānecchākṛtisaṃgateḥ // 32
27.d:
तदर्धं वाथ पञ्चाशद्युक्तं तत्परिकल्पयेत् ।
वक्त्राणि पञ्च चित्स्पन्दज्ञानेच्छाकृतिसंगतेः ॥ 32
27.m: or half of that [twenty-seven], or one should construct it endowed with fifty [beads]. / There are five faces, due to union with the vibration of consciousness, knowledge, will, and action;

27.s:
pañcadhādyantagaṃ caikyamityupāntyākṣago vidhiḥ /
śaktitadvatprabhedena tatra dvairūpyamucyate // 33
27.d:
पञ्चधाद्यन्तगं चैक्यमित्युपान्त्याक्षगो विधिः ।
शक्तितद्वत्प्रभेदेन तत्र द्वैरूप्यमुच्यते ॥ 33
27.m: or unity at the beginning and the end in fivefold manner—such is the rule regarding the penultimate bead. / A duality is stated there according to the distinction of power and the possessor of power;

27.s:
tato dviguṇamāne tu dvirūpaṃ nyāsamācaret /
tato'pi dviguṇe sṛṣṭisaṃhṛtidvitayena tam // 34
27.d:
ततो द्विगुणमाने तु द्विरूपं न्यासमाचरेत् ।
ततोऽपि द्विगुणे सृष्टिसंहृतिद्वितयेन तम् ॥ 34
27.m: in the case of double the measure, one should perform a twofold placement; / in the case of double that again, [one should perform] it with the two pairs of emission and reabsorption.

27.s:
mātṛkāṃ mālinīṃ vātha nyasyetkhaśarasaṃmite /
uttame tu dvayīṃ nyasyennyasya pūrvaṃ pracoditān // 35
27.d:
मातृकां मालिनीं वाथ न्यस्येत्खशरसंमिते ।
उत्तमे तु द्वयीं न्यस्येन्न्यस्य पूर्वं प्रचोदितान् ॥ 35
27.m: Or one should place the Mātṛkā or Mālinī on [a rosary] of fifty [beads]; / but on the best one, one should place both pairs, having first placed those previously prescribed,

27.s:
dīkṣāyāṃ mukhyato mantrāṃstānpañcadaśa daiśikaḥ /
yadi vā tattvabhuvanakalāmantrapadārṇajaiḥ // 36
27.d:
दीक्षायां मुख्यतो मन्त्रांस्तान्पञ्चदश दैशिकः ।
यदि वा तत्त्वभुवनकलामन्त्रपदार्णजैः ॥ 36
27.m: the principal fifteen mantras in initiation, the master [should place]; / or if it is made with counts born from the principles, worlds, segments, mantras, words, and phonemes,

27.s:
saṃkhyābhedaiḥ kṛte sūtre taṃ taṃ nyāsaṃ guruścaret /
kṛtvākṣasūtraṃ tasyāpi sarvaṃ sthaṇḍilavadbhavet // 37
27.d:
संख्याभेदैः कृते सूत्रे तं तं न्यासं गुरुश्चरेत् ।
कृत्वाक्षसूत्रं तस्यापि सर्वं स्थण्डिलवद्भवेत् ॥ 37
27.m: the guru should perform each respective placement on the string made with these various counts. / Having made the rosary, everything for it too should be just as for the sacred ground;

27.s:
pūjitena ca tenaiva japaṃ kuryādatandritaḥ /
vidhiruktastvayaṃ śrīmanmālinīvijayottare // 38
27.d:
पूजितेन च तेनैव जपं कुर्यादतन्द्रितः ।
विधिरुक्तस्त्वयं श्रीमन्मालिनीविजयोत्तरे ॥ 38
27.m: and with that very [rosary] worshipped, one should perform recitation unweariedly. / This rule was taught in the venerable Mālinīvijayottara:

27.s:
cakravadbhramayannetadyadvakti sa japo bhavet /
yadīkṣate juhotyetadbodhāgnau saṃpraveśanāt // 39
27.d:
चक्रवद्भ्रमयन्नेतद्यद्वक्ति स जपो भवेत् ।
यदीक्षते जुहोत्येतद्बोधाग्नौ संप्रवेशनात् ॥ 39
27.m: Turning this like a wheel, whatever he speaks becomes recitation; / whatever he sees, he offers into the fire, because of entering into the fire of consciousness.

27.s:
athavārghamahāpātraṃ kuryāttaccottaraṃ param /
nārikelamatho bailvaṃ sauvarṇaṃ rājataṃ ca vā // 40
27.d:
अथवार्घमहापात्रं कुर्यात्तच्चोत्तरं परम् ।
नारिकेलमथो बैल्वं सौवर्णं राजतं च वा ॥ 40
27.m: Alternatively, one should make a great vessel of offering, which is supreme and excellent: / of coconut, or bilva fruit, or made of gold or silver.

27.s:
tasyāpyeṣa vidhiḥ sarvaḥ pratiṣṭhādau prakīrtitaḥ /
tanniṣkamparasaiḥ pūrṇaṃ kṛtvāsminpūjayetkramam // 41
27.d:
तस्याप्येष विधिः सर्वः प्रतिष्ठादौ प्रकीर्तितः ।
तन्निष्कम्परसैः पूर्णं कृत्वास्मिन्पूजयेत्क्रमम् ॥ 41
27.m: All of this rule previously proclaimed for consecration and so forth applies to it as well. / Having filled it with unblemished sap, one should worship the transmission in it.

27.s:
adhomukhaṃ sadā sthāpyaṃ pūjitaṃ pūjane punaḥ /
tatpātramunmukhaṃ tacca riktaṃ kuryānna tādṛśam // 42
27.d:
अधोमुखं सदा स्थाप्यं पूजितं पूजने पुनः ।
तत्पात्रमुन्मुखं तच्च रिक्तं कुर्यान्न तादृशम् ॥ 42
27.m: It should always be kept turned downwards when worshipped; but at the time of worship / that vessel is turned upwards, and one should never leave such [a vessel] empty.

27.s:
pūjānte tadrasāpūrṇamātmānaṃ pravidhāya tat /
adhomukhaṃ ca saṃpūjya sthāpayet vicakṣaṇaḥ // 43
27.d:
पूजान्ते तद्रसापूर्णमात्मानं प्रविधाय तत् ।
अधोमुखं च संपूज्य स्थापयेत् विचक्षणः ॥ 43
27.m: At the end of the worship, having completely filled oneself with that sap, / the discerning one should worship it and place it turned downwards.

27.s:
khaṅgaṃ kṛpāṇikāṃ yadvā kartarīṃ makuraṃ ca vā /
vimalaṃ tattathā kuryācchrīmatkālīmukhoditam // 44
27.d:
खङ्गं कृपाणिकां यद्वा कर्तरीं मकुरं च वा ।
विमलं तत्तथा कुर्याच्छ्रीमत्कालीमुखोदितम् ॥ 44
27.m: Or a sword, a dagger, a pair of scissors, or a mirror, / flawless—one should make it just so, as taught in the venerable Kālīmukha.

27.s:
śrībhairavakule'pyuktaṃ kulaparvaprapūjane /
sthaṇḍile'gnau paṭe liṅge pātre padme'tha maṇḍale // 45
27.d:
श्रीभैरवकुलेऽप्युक्तं कुलपर्वप्रपूजने ।
स्थण्डिलेऽग्नौ पटे लिङ्गे पात्रे पद्मेऽथ मण्डले ॥ 45
27.m: It is also taught in the venerable Bhairavakula regarding the worship on Kula festival days: / 'On sacred ground, in fire, on cloth, on a liṅga, in a vessel, on a lotus, or in a maṇḍala,

27.s:
mūrtau ghaṭe'strasaṃghāte dhaṭe sūtre'tha pūjayet /
svena svenopacāreṇa saṅkaraṃ varjayediti // 46
27.d:
मूर्तौ घटेऽस्त्रसंघाते धटे सूत्रेऽथ पूजयेत् ।
स्वेन स्वेनोपचारेण सङ्करं वर्जयेदिति ॥ 46
27.m: in an image, in a jar, in an array of weapons, in a balance, or on a cord, one should worship, / each with its own service, and one should avoid confusion.'

27.s:
yathāpsu śāntaye mantrāstadvadastrādiṣu dhruvam /
śatrucchedādikartāraḥ kāmyo'taḥ saṅkarojjhitaḥ // 47
27.d:
यथाप्सु शान्तये मन्त्रास्तद्वदस्त्रादिषु ध्रुवम् ।
शत्रुच्छेदादिकर्तारः काम्योऽतः सङ्करोज्झितः ॥ 47
27.m: Just as mantras in water are surely for pacification, so [in weapons] they effect the destruction of enemies and the like; / therefore, the desire-driven rite is free from confusion.

27.s:
akāmasya tu te tattatsthānopādhivaśāddhruvam /
pāśakartanasaṃśuddhatattvāpyāyādikāriṇaḥ // 48
27.d:
अकामस्य तु ते तत्तत्स्थानोपाधिवशाद्ध्रुवम् ।
पाशकर्तनसंशुद्धतत्त्वाप्यायादिकारिणः ॥ 48
27.m: For one free of desire, however, through the force of the conditions of each respective locus, they surely / effect the severing of bonds, the nourishment of purified principles, and the like.

27.s:
athavā pustakaṃ tādṛgrahaḥśāstrakramombhitam /
suśuddhaṃ dīkṣitakṛtaṃ tatrāpyeṣa vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ // 49
27.d:
अथवा पुस्तकं तादृग्रहःशास्त्रक्रमोम्भितम् ।
सुशुद्धं दीक्षितकृतं तत्राप्येष विधिः स्मृतः ॥ 49
27.m: Alternatively, [one may worship] a book composed of the transmission of such secret scriptures, / thoroughly purified, made by an initiate; there too this rule is taught.

27.s:
itthaṃ svayaṃpratiṣṭheṣu yāvadyāvatsthitirbhavet /
vibhavaistarpaṇaṃ śuddhistāvadvicchedavarjanam // 50
27.d:
इत्थं स्वयंप्रतिष्ठेषु यावद्यावत्स्थितिर्भवेत् ।
विभवैस्तर्पणं शुद्धिस्तावद्विच्छेदवर्जनम् ॥ 50
27.m: In this way, as long as there is maintenance in things consecrated by oneself, / so long should there be propitiation with riches, purification, and the avoidance of interruption.

27.s:
ata eva yadā bhūridinaṃ maṇḍalakalpanam /
tadā dine dine kuryādvibhavaistarpaṇaṃ bahu // 51
27.d:
अत एव यदा भूरिदिनं मण्डलकल्पनम् ।
तदा दिने दिने कुर्याद्विभवैस्तर्पणं बहु ॥ 51
27.m: For this very reason, when the arrangement of the maṇḍala is for many days, / then day after day one should perform abundant propitiation with riches.

27.s:
pratiṣṭhāyāṃ ca sarvatra guruḥ pūrvoditaṃ param /
satattvamanusandhāya saṃnidhiṃ sphuṭamācaret // 52
27.d:
प्रतिष्ठायां च सर्वत्र गुरुः पूर्वोदितं परम् ।
सतत्त्वमनुसन्धाय संनिधिं स्फुटमाचरेत् ॥ 52
27.m: And in consecration everywhere, the guru, having meditated upon the supreme / reality stated before, should distinctly effect the divine presence.

27.s:
siddhe tu tanmayībhāve phale putrakasādhakaiḥ /
anyasmai taddvayādanyatarasmai tatsamarpyate // 53
27.d:
सिद्धे तु तन्मयीभावे फले पुत्रकसाधकैः ।
अन्यस्मै तद्द्वयादन्यतरस्मै तत्समर्प्यते ॥ 53
27.m: When identity with That has been achieved as the fruit, it is surrendered by spiritual sons and adepts / to another, to either one of those two.

27.s:
tasyāpyeṣa vidhiḥ sarvastadalābhe tu sarvathā /
agādhe'mbhasi tatkṣepyaṃ kṣamayitvā visṛjya ca // 54
27.d:
तस्याप्येष विधिः सर्वस्तदलाभे तु सर्वथा ।
अगाधेऽम्भसि तत्क्षेप्यं क्षमयित्वा विसृज्य च ॥ 54
27.m: For that [recipient] as well, all of this rule applies; but in the event of its complete absence, / having asked for forgiveness and dismissed it, it should be thrown into deep water.

27.s:
ityeṣa svapratiṣṭhānavidhiḥ śivanirūpitaḥ /
parapratiṣṭhite liṅge bāṇīye'tha svayaṃbhuvi // 55
27.d:
इत्येष स्वप्रतिष्ठानविधिः शिवनिरूपितः ।
परप्रतिष्ठिते लिङ्गे बाणीयेऽथ स्वयंभुवि ॥ 55
27.m: Thus this rule of self-consecration has been expounded by Śiva. / On a liṅga consecrated by another, or a Bāṇa-liṅga, or a self-manifested one,

27.s:
sarvamāsanapakṣe prāṅnyasya saṃpūjayetkramam /
śuddhāśuddhādhvajāḥ sarve mantrāḥ sarvaḥ śivāntakaḥ // 56
27.d:
सर्वमासनपक्षे प्राङ्न्यस्य संपूजयेत्क्रमम् ।
शुद्धाशुद्धाध्वजाः सर्वे मन्त्राः सर्वः शिवान्तकः ॥ 56
27.m: having first placed everything on the seat, one should worship the transmission. / All mantras belonging to the pure and impure paths, and all ending with Śiva,

27.s:
adhvā cehāsane proktastatsarvatrārcayedidam /
āvāhanavisṛṣṭī tu tatra prāgvatsamācaret // 57
27.d:
अध्वा चेहासने प्रोक्तस्तत्सर्वत्रार्चयेदिदम् ।
आवाहनविसृष्टी तु तत्र प्राग्वत्समाचरेत् ॥ 57
27.m: the path taught here upon the seat—all this one should worship everywhere; / but invocation and dismissal should be performed there as before.

27.s:
uktaṃ tantre'pyaghoreśe svacchande vibhunā tathā /
athavā pratyahaṃ proktamānārdhārdhaniyogataḥ // 58
27.d:
उक्तं तन्त्रेऽप्यघोरेशे स्वच्छन्दे विभुना तथा ।
अथवा प्रत्यहं प्रोक्तमानार्धार्धनियोगतः ॥ 58
27.m: It is likewise taught by the Lord in the Tantra of Aghoreśa, the Svacchanda; / or, having made whatever desired maṇḍala every day

27.s:
kṛtveṣṭaṃ maṇḍalaṃ tatra samastaṃ kramamarcayet /
bahuprakārabhinnasya liṅgasyārcā nirūpitā // 59
27.d:
कृत्वेष्टं मण्डलं तत्र समस्तं क्रममर्चयेत् ।
बहुप्रकारभिन्नस्य लिङ्गस्यार्चा निरूपिता ॥ 59
27.m: according to the prescription of half-and-half portions taught [there], one should worship the whole transmission. / Thus the worship of the liṅga, divided into many kinds, has been expounded.
